cards.back: a social process by which individual groups obtain what they need and want through creating offerings and freely exchanging products and services of value with others
cards.quote: a social process by which individual groups obtain what they need and want through creating offerings and freely exchanging products and services of value with others
cards.note: Marketing = people getting what they need and want by creating and freely exchanging things of value.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define marketing in the traditional sense (functions view).
cards.back: marketing has been referred to as performance of business activities that direct the flow of goods and services from producers to consumers.
cards.quote: marketing has been referred to as performance of business activities that direct the flow of goods and services from producers to consumers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Is marketing only a post-production activity? What does it include?
cards.back: Marketing is not merely a post-production activity. It includes many activities that are performed even before goods are actually produced and continue even after the goods have been sold.
cards.quote: Marketing is not merely a post-production activity. It includes many activities that are performed even before goods are actually produced and continue even after the goods have been sold.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a market in the traditional sense?
cards.back: In the traditional sense, the term ‘market’ refers to the place where buyers and sellers gather to enter into transactions involving the exchange of goods and services.
cards.quote: In the traditional sense, the term ‘market’ refers to the place where buyers and sellers gather to enter into transactions involving the exchange of goods and services.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does 'market' mean in the modern marketing sense?
cards.back: But in modern marketing sense, the term market has a broader meaning. It refers to a set of actual and potential buyers of a product or service.
cards.quote: But in modern marketing sense, the term market has a broader meaning. It refers to a set of actual and potential buyers of a product or service.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define a need.
cards.back: A need is a state of felt deprivation or feeling of being deprived of something.
cards.quote: A need is a state of felt deprivation or feeling of being deprived of something.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define wants.
cards.back: Wants, on the other hand, are culturally defined objects that are potential satisfiers of needs. In other words, human needs shaped by such factors as culture, personality and religion are called wants.
cards.quote: Wants, on the other hand, are culturally defined objects that are potential satisfiers of needs. In other words, human needs shaped by such factors as culture, personality and religion are called wants.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a market offering?
cards.back: Market offering refers to a complete offer for a product or service, having given features like size, quality, taste, etc; at a certain price; available at a given outlet or location and so on.
cards.quote: Market offering refers to a complete offer for a product or service, having given features like size, quality, taste, etc; at a certain price; available at a given outlet or location and so on.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Exchange is, therefore, referred to as the ____ of marketing.
cards.back: Exchange is, therefore, referred to as the **essence** of marketing.
cards.quote: Exchange is, therefore, referred to as the essence of marketing.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define exchange.
cards.back: Exchange refers to the process through which two or more parties come together to obtain the desired product or service from someone, offering the same by giving something in return.
cards.quote: Exchange refers to the process through which two or more parties come together to obtain the desired product or service from someone, offering the same by giving something in return.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five conditions that must be satisfied for an exchange to take place.
cards.back:
(i) Involvement of at least two parties viz., the buyer and the seller.
(ii) Each party should be capable of offering something of value to the other.
(iii) Each party should have the ability to communicate and deliver the product or service.
(iv) Each party should have freedom to accept or reject other party's offer.
(v) The parties should be willing to enter into transaction with each other.
cards.quote: (i) Involvement of at least two parties viz., the buyer and the seller. (ii) Each party should be capable of offering something of value to the other. For example, the seller offers a product and the buyer, money. (iii) Each party should have the ability to communicate and deliver the product or service. No exchange can take place if the buyers and sellers are not able to communicate with each other or if they can not deliver something of value to the other. (iv) Each party should have freedom to accept or reject other party's offer. (v) The parties should be willing to enter into transaction with each other. Thus, the acceptance or rejection of the offer takes place on voluntary basis rather than on the bases of any compulsion.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is marketing management?
cards.back: Marketing management means management of the marketing function. In other words, marketing management refers to planning, organising, directing and control of the activities which facilitate exchange of goods and services between producers and consumers or users of products and services.
cards.quote: Marketing management means management of the marketing function. In other words, marketing management refers to planning, organising, directing and control of the activities which facilitate exchange of goods and services between producers and consumers or users of products and services.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define marketing management (Philip Kotler).
cards.back: the art and science of choosing target markets and getting, keeping and growing customers through creating, delivering and communicating superior customer values
cards.quote: the art and science of choosing target markets and getting, keeping and growing customers through creating, delivering and communicating superior customer values

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Whose definition: planning and executing the conception, pricing, promotion and distribution of ideas, goods and services?
cards.back: …the conception, pricing, promotion and distribution of ideas, goods and services to create exchanges that satisfy individual and organisational goals" by American Management Association
cards.quote: the conception, pricing, promotion and distribution of ideas, goods and services to create exchanges that satisfy individual and organisational goals" by American Management Association

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Overfull demand: what is the marketing manager's job?
cards.back: The job of marketing mangers, in these situations would be to find ways to reduce the demand temporarily by say reducing the expenditure on promotion or increasing the prices.
cards.quote: The job of marketing mangers, in these situations would be to find ways to reduce the demand temporarily by say reducing the expenditure on promotion or increasing the prices.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Marketing vs selling: the difference in scope.
cards.back:
marketing involves whole range of activities relating to planning, pricing, promoting and distributing the products that satisfy customer's needs.
The function of selling, on the other hand, is restricted to promotion of goods and services through salesmanship, advertising, publicity and short-term incentives so that title of the product is transferred from seller to buyer or in other words product is converted into cash.
cards.quote: In short, marketing involves whole range of activities relating to planning, pricing, promoting and distributing the products that satisfy customer's needs. The function of selling, on the other hand, is restricted to promotion of goods and services through salesmanship, advertising, publicity and short-term incentives so that title of the product is transferred from seller to buyer or in other words product is converted into cash.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Marketing refers to a large set of activities of which ____ is just one part.
cards.back: Marketing refers to a large set of activities of which **selling** is just one part.
cards.quote: Marketing refers to a large set of activities of which selling is just one part.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Under the production concept, what was considered the key to the success of a firm?
cards.back: Thus, availability and affordability of the product were considered to be the key to the success of a firm.
cards.quote: Thus, availability and affordability of the product were considered to be the key to the success of a firm.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Under the production concept, how was it believed that profits could be maximised?
cards.back: It was believed that profits could be maximised by producing at large scale, thereby reducing the average cost of production.
cards.quote: It was believed that profits could be maximised by producing at large scale, thereby reducing the average cost of production.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Under the product concept, what became the key to profit maximisation of a firm?
cards.back: Thus, product improvement became the key to profit maximisation of a firm, under the concept of product orientation.
cards.quote: Thus, product improvement became the key to profit maximisation of a firm, under the concept of product orientation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Under the selling concept, what must firms undertake to make customers buy their products?
cards.back: Therefore, firms must undertake aggressive selling and promotional efforts to make customers buy their products.
cards.quote: Therefore, firms must undertake aggressive selling and promotional efforts to make customers buy their products.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Marketing orientation implies that focus on ____ of customer's needs is the key to the success of any organisation in the market.
cards.back: Marketing orientation implies that focus on **satisfaction** of customer's needs is the key to the success of any organisation in the market.
cards.quote: Marketing orientation implies that focus on satisfaction of customer's needs is the key to the success of any organisation in the market.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The basic role of a firm then is to ‘____ a need and ____ it’.
cards.back: The basic role of a firm then is to ‘**identify** a need and **fill** it’.
cards.quote: The basic role of a firm then is to ‘identify a need and fill it’.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five pillars of the marketing concept.
cards.back:
(i) Identification of market or customer who are chosen as the target of marketing effort.
(ii) Understanding needs and wants of customers in the target market.
(iii) Development of products or services for satisfying needs of the target market.
(iv) Satisfying needs of target market better than the competitors.
(v) Doing all this at a profit.
cards.quote: (i) Identification of market or customer who are chosen as the target of marketing effort. (ii) Understanding needs and wants of customers in the target market. (iii) Development of products or services for satisfying needs of the target market. (iv) Satisfying needs of target market better than the competitors. (v) Doing all this at a profit.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is the focus of the marketing concept?
cards.back: Thus, the focus of the marketing concept is on customer needs and the customer satisfaction becomes the means to achieving the firms' objective of maximising profit.
cards.quote: Thus, the focus of the marketing concept is on customer needs and the customer satisfaction becomes the means to achieving the firms' objective of maximising profit.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define the societal marketing concept.
cards.back: The societal marketing concept holds that the task of any organisation is to identify the needs and wants of the target market and deliver the desired satisfaction in an effective and efficient manner so that the long-term well-being of the consumers and the society is taken care of.
cards.quote: The societal marketing concept holds that the task of any organisation is to identify the needs and wants of the target market and deliver the desired satisfaction in an effective and efficient manner so that the long-term well-being of the consumers and the society is taken care of.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: How is the societal marketing concept related to the marketing concept?
cards.back: Thus, the societal marketing concept is the extension of the marketing concept as supplemented by the concern for the long-term welfare of the society.
cards.quote: Thus, the societal marketing concept is the extension of the marketing concept as supplemented by the concern for the long-term welfare of the society.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define standardisation.
cards.back: Standardisation refers to producing goods of predetermined specifications, which helps in achieving uniformity and consistency in the output.
cards.quote: Standardisation refers to producing goods of predetermined specifications, which helps in achieving uniformity and consistency in the output.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define grading.
cards.back: Grading is the process of classification of products into different groups, on the basis of some of its important characteristics such as quality, size, etc.
cards.quote: Grading is the process of classification of products into different groups, on the basis of some of its important characteristics such as quality, size, etc.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Packaging and labelling have become so important in modern day marketing that these are considered as the ____ of marketing.
cards.back: Packaging and labelling have become so important in modern day marketing that these are considered as the **pillars** of marketing.
cards.quote: Packaging and labelling have become so important in modern day marketing that these are considered as the pillars of marketing.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is labelling?
cards.back: Labelling refers to designing and developing the label to be put on the package.
cards.quote: Labelling refers to designing and developing the label to be put on the package.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Customer support services are very effective in bringing ____ from the customers and developing brand loyality for a product.
cards.back: Customer support services are very effective in bringing **repeat sales** from the customers and developing brand loyality for a product.
cards.quote: Customer support services are very effective in bringing repeat sales from the customers and developing brand loyality for a product.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four elements (four Ps) of the marketing mix.
cards.back:
(i) Product
(ii) Price
(iii) Place
(iv) Promotion
cards.quote: The marketing mix consists of various elements, which have broadly been classified into four categories, popularly known as four Ps of marketing. These are: (i) Product, (ii) Price, (iii) Place, and (iv) Promotion.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a product (first P of the marketing mix)?
cards.back: Product means goods or services or ‘anything of value’, which is offered to the market for sale.
cards.quote: Product means goods or services or ‘anything of value’, which is offered to the market for sale.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is price (second P of the marketing mix)?
cards.back: Price is the amount of money customers have to pay to obtain the product.
cards.quote: Price is the amount of money customers have to pay to obtain the product.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is place (third P of the marketing mix)?
cards.back: Place or Physical Distribution include activities that make firm's products available to the target customers.
cards.quote: Place or Physical Distribution include activities that make firm's products available to the target customers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is promotion (fourth P of the marketing mix)?
cards.back: Promotion of products and services include activities that communicate availability, features, merits, etc., of the products to the target customers and persuade them to buy it.
cards.quote: Promotion of products and services include activities that communicate availability, features, merits, etc., of the products to the target customers and persuade them to buy it.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define a product from the customer's point of view.
cards.back: From the customer's point of view, a product is a bundle of utilities, which is purchased because of its capability to provide satisfaction of certain need.
cards.quote: From the customer's point of view, a product is a bundle of utilities, which is purchased because of its capability to provide satisfaction of certain need.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the three types of benefits a customer may seek from a product.
cards.back:
(i) functional benefits
(ii) psychological benefits
(iii) social benefits
cards.quote: There can be three types of benefits a customer may seek to satisfy from the purchase of a product, viz., (i) functional benefits, (ii) psychological benefits, and (iii) social benefits.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Into what two broad categories are products classified?
cards.back:
(i) consumers' products
(ii) industrial products
cards.quote: Products may broadly be classified into two categories -- (i) consumers' products, and (ii) industrial products.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are consumer products?
cards.back: Products, which are purchased by the ultimate consumers or users for satisfying their personal needs and desires are referred to as consumer products.
cards.quote: Products, which are purchased by the ultimate consumers or users for satisfying their personal needs and desires are referred to as consumer products.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are convenience products?
cards.back: Those consumer products, which are purchased frequently, immediately and with least time and efforts are referred to as convenience goods.
cards.quote: Those consumer products, which are purchased frequently, immediately and with least time and efforts are referred to as convenience goods.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: By shopping effort: cigarettes, ice creams, medicines, newspaper and stationery are which type of consumer product?
cards.back: Those consumer products, which are purchased frequently, immediately and with least time and efforts are referred to as convenience goods. Examples of such products are cigarettes, ice creams, medicines, newspaper, stationery items toothpaste etc.
cards.quote: Those consumer products, which are purchased frequently, immediately and with least time and efforts are referred to as convenience goods. Examples of such products are cigarettes, ice creams, medicines, newspaper, stationery items toothpaste etc.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are shopping products?
cards.back: Shopping products are those consumer goods where buyers devote considerable time, to compare the quality, price, style, suitability, etc., at several stores, before making final purchase.
cards.quote: Shopping products are those consumer goods where buyers devote considerable time, to compare the quality, price, style, suitability, etc., at several stores, before making final purchase.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: By shopping effort: clothes, shoes, jewellery, furniture, radio and television are which type of consumer product?
cards.back: Shopping products are those consumer goods where buyers devote considerable time, to compare the quality, price, style, suitability, etc., at several stores, before making final purchase. Some of the examples of shopping products are clothes, shoes, jewellery, furniture, radio, television, etc.
cards.quote: Shopping products are those consumer goods where buyers devote considerable time, to compare the quality, price, style, suitability, etc., at several stores, before making final purchase. Some of the examples of shopping products are clothes, shoes, jewellery, furniture, radio, television, etc.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Speciality products are those consumer goods that have what features, and what level of brand loyalty?
cards.back: which have certain special features because of which people make special efforts in their purchase. These products are such, which have reached a brand loyalty of the highest order, with a significant number of buyers.
cards.quote: which have certain special features because of which people make special efforts in their purchase. These products are such, which have reached a brand loyalty of the highest order, with a significant number of buyers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The demand for these goods is relatively ____, i.e., even if the price is increased, the demand does not come down.
cards.back: The demand for these goods is relatively **inelastic**, i.e., even if the price is increased, the demand does not come down.
cards.quote: The demand for these goods is relatively inelastic, i.e., even if the price is increased, the demand does not come down.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: On the basis of durability, how are consumer products classified?
cards.back:
Durable
Non-durable
Services
cards.quote: On the basis of their durability, the consumer products have been classified into three categories-- Durable, Non-durable and Services.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are non-durable products?
cards.back: The consumer products which are normally consumed in one or few uses are called non-durable products.
cards.quote: The consumer products which are normally consumed in one or few uses are called non-durable products.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Non-durable products: what margin, availability and advertising do they need?
cards.back: From the marketing point of view, these products generally command a small margin, should be made available in many locations and need to be heavily advertised.
cards.quote: From the marketing point of view, these products generally command a small margin, should be made available in many locations and need to be heavily advertised.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are durable products?
cards.back: Those tangible consumer products which normally survive many years
cards.quote: Those tangible consumer products which normally survive many years

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Durable products: what margin and seller support do they need?
cards.back: These goods are generally used for a longer period, command a higher per unit margin, require greater personal-selling efforts, guarantees and after sales services, on the part of the seller.
cards.quote: These goods are generally used for a longer period, command a higher per unit margin, require greater personal-selling efforts, guarantees and after sales services, on the part of the seller.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What do we mean by services?
cards.back: By services we mean those intangible activities, benefits which are offered for sale, e.g., dry cleaning, watch repairs, hair cutting, postal services, services offered by a doctor, an architect and a lawyer.
cards.quote: By services we mean those intangible activities, benefits which are offered for sale, e.g., dry cleaning, watch repairs, hair cutting, postal services, services offered by a doctor, an architect and a lawyer.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are industrial products?
cards.back: Industrial products are those products, which are used as inputs in producing other products.
cards.quote: Industrial products are those products, which are used as inputs in producing other products.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are 'Materials and Parts' among industrial goods?
cards.back: Materials and Parts: These include goods that enter the manufacture's products completely.
cards.quote: Materials and Parts: These include goods that enter the manufacture's products completely.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are 'Capital Items' among industrial goods?
cards.back: Capital Items: These are such goods that are used in the production of finished goods.
cards.quote: Capital Items: These are such goods that are used in the production of finished goods.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are 'Supplies and Business Services' among industrial goods?
cards.back: Supplies and Business Services: These are short lasting goods and services that facilitate developing or managing the finished product.
cards.quote: Supplies and Business Services: These are short lasting goods and services that facilitate developing or managing the finished product.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is branding?
cards.back: This process of giving a name or a sign or a symbol etc., to a product is called branding.
cards.quote: This process of giving a name or a sign or a symbol etc., to a product is called branding.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a generic name?
cards.back: Generic name refers to the name of the whole class of the product.
cards.quote: Generic name refers to the name of the whole class of the product.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define a brand.
cards.back: A brand is a name, term, sign, symbol, design or some combination of them, used to identify the products-- goods or services of one seller or group of sellers and to differentiate them from those of the competitors.
cards.quote: A brand is a name, term, sign, symbol, design or some combination of them, used to identify the products-- goods or services of one seller or group of sellers and to differentiate them from those of the competitors.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a brand name?
cards.back: That part of a brand, which can be spoken, is called a brand name. In other words, brand name is the verbal component of a brand.
cards.quote: That part of a brand, which can be spoken, is called a brand name. In other words, brand name is the verbal component of a brand.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a brand mark?
cards.back: That part of a brand which can be recognised but which is not utterable is called brand mark. It appears in the form of a symbol, design, distinct colour scheme or lettering.
cards.quote: That part of a brand which can be recognised but which is not utterable is called brand mark. It appears in the form of a symbol, design, distinct colour scheme or lettering.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a trade mark?
cards.back: A brand or part of a brand that is given legal protection is called trademark. The protection is given against its use by other firms.
cards.quote: A brand or part of a brand that is given legal protection is called trademark. The protection is given against its use by other firms.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the seven characteristics of a good brand name.
cards.back:
(i) The brand name should be short, easy to pronounce, spell, recognise and remember
(ii) A brand should suggest the product's benefits and qualities.
(iii) A brand name should be distinctive.
(iv) The brand name should be adaptable to packing or labelling requirements, to different advertising media and to different languages.
(v) The brand name should be sufficiently versatile to accommodate new products, which are added to the product line.
(vi) It should be capable of being registered and protected legally.
(vii) Chosen name should have staying power i.e., it should not get out of date.
cards.quote: (i) The brand name should be short, easy to pronounce, spell, recognise and remember e.g., Ponds, VIP, Rin, Vim, etc. (ii) A brand should suggest the product's benefits and qualities. It should be appropriate to the product's function. (iii) A brand name should be distinctive. (iv) The brand name should be adaptable to packing or labelling requirements, to different advertising media and to different languages. (v) The brand name should be sufficiently versatile to accommodate new products, which are added to the product line. (vi) It should be capable of being registered and protected legally. (vii) Chosen name should have staying power i.e., it should not get out of date.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is packaging?
cards.back: Packaging refers to the act of designing and producing the container or wrapper of a product.
cards.quote: Packaging refers to the act of designing and producing the container or wrapper of a product.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the three levels of packaging.
cards.back:
1. Primary Package: It refers to the product's immediate container.
2. Secondary Packaging: It refers to additional layers of protection that are kept till the product is ready for use
3. Transportation Packaging: It refers to further packaging components necessary for storage, identification or transportation.
cards.quote: There can be three different levels of packaging. These are as below: 1. Primary Package: It refers to the product's immediate container. In some cases, the primary package is kept till the consumer is ready to use the product (e.g., plastic packet for socks); whereas in other cases, it is kept throughout the entire life of the product (e.g., a toothpaste tube, a match box, etc.). 2. Secondary Packaging: It refers to additional layers of protection that are kept till the product is ready for use, e.g., a tube of shaving cream usually comes in a card board box. When consumers start using the shaving cream, they will dispose off the box but retain the primary tube. 3. Transportation Packaging: It refers to further packaging components necessary for storage, identification or transportation. For example, a toothpaste manufacturer may send the goods to retailers in corrugated boxes containing 10, 20, or 100 units.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name four reasons why packaging is important in marketing.
cards.back:
(i) Rising Standards of Health and Sanitation
(ii) Self Service Outlets
(iii) Innovational Opportunity
(iv) Product Differentiation
cards.quote: (i) Rising Standards of Health and Sanitation: Because of the increasing standards of living in the country, more and more people have started purchasing packed goods as the chances of adulteration in such goods are minimised. (ii) Self Service Outlets: The self-service retail outlets are becoming very popular, particularly in major cities and towns. Because of this, some of the traditional role assigned to personal selling in respect of promotion has gone to packaging. (iii) Innovational Opportunity: Some of the recent developments in the area of packaging have completely changed the marketing scene in the country. For example, milk can now be stored for 4-5 days without refrigeration in the recently developed packing materials. Similarly, in the area of pharmaceuticals, soft drinks, etc., lots of new innovations have come in respect of packaging. As a result, the scope for the marketing of such products has increased. (iv) Product Differentiation: Packaging is one of the very important means of creating product differentiation. The colour, size, material, etc., of package makes real difference in the perception of customers about the quality of the product. For example, by looking at the package of a product say Paint or Hair Oil, one can make some guess about quality of the product contained in it.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Another important function of labeling is to provide information required by ____.
cards.back: Another important function of labeling is to provide information required by **law**.
cards.quote: Another important function of labeling is to provide information required by law.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define price.
cards.back: Price may therefore be defined as the amount of money paid by a buyer (or received by a seller) in consideration of the purchase of a product or a services.
cards.quote: Price may therefore be defined as the amount of money paid by a buyer (or received by a seller) in consideration of the purchase of a product or a services.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Which factor is an effective competitive weapon and the single most important factor in a firm's revenue and profits?
cards.back: Pricing is considered to be an effective competitive weapon. In the conditions of perfect competition, most of the firms compete with each other on the basis of this factor. It is also the single most important factor affecting the revenue and profits of a firm.
cards.quote: Pricing is considered to be an effective competitive weapon. In the conditions of perfect competition, most of the firms compete with each other on the basis of this factor. It is also the single most important factor affecting the revenue and profits of a firm.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the three types of costs.
cards.back:
Fixed Costs
Variable Costs
Semi Variable Costs
cards.quote: There are broadly three types of costs: viz., Fixed Costs, Variable Costs and Semi Variable Costs.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are fixed costs?
cards.back: Fixed costs are those costs, which do not vary with the level of activity of a firm say with the volume of production or sale.
cards.quote: Fixed costs are those costs, which do not vary with the level of activity of a firm say with the volume of production or sale.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are variable costs?
cards.back: Those costs which vary in direct proportion with the level of activity are called variable costs.
cards.quote: Those costs which vary in direct proportion with the level of activity are called variable costs.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are semi variable costs?
cards.back: Semi variable costs are those costs which vary with the level of activity but not in direct proportion with it.
cards.quote: Semi variable costs are those costs which vary with the level of activity but not in direct proportion with it.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are total costs?
cards.back: Total Costs are the sum total of the fixed, variable and semi-variable costs for the specific level of activity, say volume of sales or quantity produced.
cards.quote: Total Costs are the sum total of the fixed, variable and semi-variable costs for the specific level of activity, say volume of sales or quantity produced.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The cost sets the minimum level or the ____ at which the product may be sold.
cards.back: The cost sets the minimum level or the **floor price** at which the product may be sold.
cards.quote: The cost sets the minimum level or the floor price at which the product may be sold.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In pricing, what sets the lower limit of the price and what sets the upper limit?
cards.back: While the product costs set the lower limits of the price, the utility provided by the product and the intensity of demand of the buyer sets the upper limit of price, which a buyer would be prepared to pay.
cards.quote: While the product costs set the lower limits of the price, the utility provided by the product and the intensity of demand of the buyer sets the upper limit of price, which a buyer would be prepared to pay.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Government can declare a product as ____ product and regulate its price.
cards.back: Government can declare a product as **essential** product and regulate its price.
cards.quote: Government can declare a product as essential product and regulate its price.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Apart from profit maximisation, name the pricing objectives a firm may have.
cards.back:
(a) Obtaining Market Share Leadership
(b) Surviving in a Competitive Market
(c) Attaining Product Quality Leadership
cards.quote: Apart from profit maximisation, the pricing objectives of a firm may include: (a) Obtaining Market Share Leadership: If a firms objective is to obtain larger share of the market; it will keep the price of its products at lower levels so that greater number of people are attracted to purchase the products; (b) Surviving in a Competitive Market: If a firm is facing difficulties in surviving in the market because of intense competition or introduction of a more efficient substitute by a competitor, it may resort to discounting its products or running a promotion campaign to liquidate its stock; and (c) Attaining Product Quality Leadership: In this case, normally higher prices are charged to cover high quality and high cost of research and Development.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is physical distribution?
cards.back: The physical handling and movement of goods from place of production to the place of distribution is referred to as physical distribution, which is a very important element of marketing mix.
cards.quote: The physical handling and movement of goods from place of production to the place of distribution is referred to as physical distribution, which is a very important element of marketing mix.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does physical distribution cover?
cards.back: Physical distribution covers all the activities required to physically move goods from manufacturers to the customers.
cards.quote: Physical distribution covers all the activities required to physically move goods from manufacturers to the customers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: ____ is the means of carrying goods and raw materials from the point of production to the point of sale.
cards.back:
Transportation
Transportation is the means of carrying goods and raw materials from the point of production to the point of sale.
cards.quote: Transportation is the means of carrying goods and raw materials from the point of production to the point of sale.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Warehousing: how does the number of warehouses affect service time and cost?
cards.back: Generally larger the number of warehouses a firm has, lesser would be the time taken in serving customers at different locations but greater would be the cost of warehousing and vice-versa.
cards.quote: Generally larger the number of warehouses a firm has, lesser would be the time taken in serving customers at different locations but greater would be the cost of warehousing and vice-versa.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Inventory control: what does a higher level of inventory mean for service and cost?
cards.back: Higher the level of inventory, higher will be the level of service to customers but the cost of carrying the inventory will also be high because lot of capital would be tied up in the stock.
cards.quote: Higher the level of inventory, higher will be the level of service to customers but the cost of carrying the inventory will also be high because lot of capital would be tied up in the stock.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define promotion.
cards.back: Promotion refers to the use of communication with the twin objective of informing potential customers about a product and persuading them to buy it.
cards.quote: Promotion refers to the use of communication with the twin objective of informing potential customers about a product and persuading them to buy it.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is the promotion mix?
cards.back: Promotion mix refers to combination of promotional tools used by an organisation to achieve its communication objectives.
cards.quote: Promotion mix refers to combination of promotional tools used by an organisation to achieve its communication objectives.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four elements of the promotion mix.
cards.back:
(i) Advertising
(ii) Personal Selling
(iii) Sales Promotion
(iv) Publicity
cards.quote: These include: (i) Advertising, (ii) Personal Selling, (iii) Sales Promotion, and (iv) Publicity.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define advertising.
cards.back: Advertising is perhaps the most commonly used tool of promotion. It is an impersonal form of communication, which is paid for by the marketers (sponsors) to promote some goods or service.
cards.quote: Advertising is perhaps the most commonly used tool of promotion. It is an impersonal form of communication, which is paid for by the marketers (sponsors) to promote some goods or service.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the three distinguishing features of advertising.
cards.back:
(i) Paid Form: Advertising is a paid form of communication.
(ii) Impersonality: There is no direct face-to-face contact between the prospect and the advertiser.
(iii) Identified Sponsor: Advertising is undertaken by some identified individual or company
cards.quote: (i) Paid Form: Advertising is a paid form of communication. That is, the sponsor has to bear the cost of communicating with the prospects. (ii) Impersonality: There is no direct face-to-face contact between the prospect and the advertiser. It is therefore, referred to as impersonal method of promotion. Advertising creates a monologue and not a dialogue. (iii) Identified Sponsor: Advertising is undertaken by some identified individual or company, who makes the advertising efforts and also bears the cost of it.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four merits of advertising.
cards.back:
(i) Mass Reach
(ii) Enhancing Customer Satisfaction and Confidence
(iii) Expressiveness
(iv) Economy
cards.quote: (i) Mass Reach: Advertising is a medium through which a large number of people can be reached over a vast geographical area. For example, an advertisement message placed in a national daily reaches lakhs of its subscribers. (ii) Enhancing Customer Satisfaction and Confidence: Advertising creates confidence amongst prospective buyers as they feel more comfortable and assured about the product quality and hence feel more satisfied. (iii) Expressiveness: With the developments in art, computer designs, and graphics, advertising has developed into one of the most forceful medium of communication. With the special effects that can be created, even simple products and messages can look very attractive. (iv) Economy: Advertising is a very economical mode of communication if large number of people are to be reached. Because of its wide reach, the overall cost of advertising gets spread over numerous communication links established. As a result the per-unit cost of reach comes low.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Objection to advertising: 'Adds to Cost'. What do critics argue?
cards.back: The opponents of advertising argue that advertising unnecessarily adds to the cost of product, which is ultimately passed on to the buyers in the form of high prices.
cards.quote: The opponents of advertising argue that advertising unnecessarily adds to the cost of product, which is ultimately passed on to the buyers in the form of high prices.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Objection to advertising: 'Undermines Social Values'. What is the criticism?
cards.back: Another important criticism of advertising is that it undermines social values and promotes materialism.
cards.quote: Another important criticism of advertising is that it undermines social values and promotes materialism.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Objection to advertising: 'Confuses the Buyers'. What is the criticism?
cards.back: Another criticism against advertisement is that so many products are being advertised which makes similar claims that the buyer gets confused as to which one is true and which one should be relied upon.
cards.quote: Another criticism against advertisement is that so many products are being advertised which makes similar claims that the buyer gets confused as to which one is true and which one should be relied upon.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Objection to advertising: 'Encourages Sale of Inferior Products'. What is the criticism?
cards.back: Advertising does not distinguish between superior and inferior products and persuade people to purchase even the inferior products.
cards.quote: Advertising does not distinguish between superior and inferior products and persuade people to purchase even the inferior products.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the two features of personal selling.
cards.back:
(i) Personal Form: In personal selling a direct face-to-face dialogue takes place that involves an interactive relationship between the seller and the buyer.
(ii) Development of Relationship: Personal selling allows a salesperson to develop personal relationships with the prospective customers
cards.quote: (i) Personal Form: In personal selling a direct face-to-face dialogue takes place that involves an interactive relationship between the seller and the buyer. (ii) Development of Relationship: Personal selling allows a salesperson to develop personal relationships with the prospective customers, which may become important in making sale.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the three merits of personal selling.
cards.back:
(i) Flexibility
(ii) Direct Feedback
(iii) Minimum Wastage
cards.quote: (i) Flexibility: There is lot of flexibility in personal selling. The sales presentation can be adjusted to fit the specific needs of the individual customers. (ii) Direct Feedback: As there is direct face-to-face communication in personal selling, it is possible to take a direct feed back from the customer and to adapt the presentation according to the needs of the prospects. (iii) Minimum Wastage: The wastage of efforts in personal selling can be minimised as company can decide the target customers before making any contact with them.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the eight points on the importance of personal selling to businessmen.
cards.back:
(i) Effective Promotional Tool
(ii) Flexible Tool
(iii) Minimises Wastage of Efforts
(iv) Consumer Attention
(v) Lasting Relationship
(vi) Personal Rapport
(vii) Role in Introduction Stage
(viii) Link with Customers
cards.quote: (i) Effective Promotional Tool: Personal selling is very effective promotional tool, which helps in influencing the prospects about the merits of a product and thereby increasing its sale. (ii) Flexible Tool: Personal selling is more flexible than other tools of promotion such as advertising and sales promotion. It helps business persons in adopting their offer in varying purchase situations. (iii) Minimises Wastage of Efforts: Compared with other tools of promotion, the possibility of wastage of efforts in personal selling is minimum. This helps the business persons in bringing economy in their efforts. (iv) Consumer Attention: There is an opportunity to detect the loss of consumer attention and interest in a personal selling situation. This helps a business person in successfully completing the sale. (v) Lasting Relationship: Personal selling helps to develop lasting relationship between the sales persons and the customers, which is very important for achieving the objectives of business. (vi) Personal Rapport: Development of personal rapport with customers increases the competitive strength of a business organisation. (vii) Role in Introduction Stage: Personal selling plays very important role in the introduction stage of a new product as it helps in persuading customers about the merits of the product. (viii) Link with Customers: Sales people play three different roles, namely persuasive role, service role and informative role, and thereby link a business firm to its customers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four ways customers benefit from personal selling.
cards.back:
(i) Help in Identifying Needs
(ii) Latest Market Information
(iii) Expert Advice
(iv) Induces Customers
cards.quote: (i) Help in Identifying Needs: Personal selling helps the customers in identifying their needs and wants and in knowing how these can best be satisfied. (ii) Latest Market Information: Customers get latest market information regarding price changes, product availability and shortages and new product introduction, which help them in taking the purchase decisions in a better way. (iii) Expert Advice: Customers get expert advice and guidance in purchasing various goods and services, which help them in making better purchase. (iv) Induces Customers: Personal selling induces customers to purchase new products that satisfy their needs in a better way and thereby helps in improving their standards of living.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five points on the importance of personal selling to society.
cards.back:
(i) Converts Latest Demand
(ii) Employment Opportunities
(iii) Career Opportunities
(iv) Mobility of Sales People
(v) Product Standardisation
cards.quote: (i) Converts Latest Demand: Personal selling converts latest demand into effective demand. It is through this cycle that the economic activity in the society is fostered, leading to more jobs, more incomes and more products and services. That is how economic growth is influenced by personal selling. (ii) Employment Opportunities: Personal selling offers greater income and employment opportunities to the unemployed youth. (iii) Career Opportunities: Personal selling provides attractive career with greater opportunities for advancement and job satisfaction as well as security, respect, variety, interest and independence to young men and women. (iv) Mobility of Sales People: There is a greater degree of mobility in sales people, which promote travel and tourism in the country. (v) Product Standardisation: Personal selling increases product standardisation and uniformity in consumption pattern in a diverse society.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define sales promotion.
cards.back: Sales promotion refers to short-term incentives, which are designed to encourage the buyers to make immediate purchase of a product or service.
cards.quote: Sales promotion refers to short-term incentives, which are designed to encourage the buyers to make immediate purchase of a product or service.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the three merits of sales promotion.
cards.back:
(i) Attention Value
(ii) Useful in New Product Launch
(iii) Synergy in Total Promotional Efforts
cards.quote: (i) Attention Value: Sales promotion activities attract attention of the people because of the use of incentives. (ii) Useful in New Product Launch: Sales promotion tools can be very effective at the time of introduction of a new product in the market. It induces people to break away from their regular buying behaviour and try the new product. (iii) Synergy in Total Promotional Efforts: Sales promotion activities are designed to supplement the personal selling and advertising efforts used by a firm and add to the over all effectiveness of the promotional efforts of a firm.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Sales promotion limitation: 'Reflects Crisis'. What does it mean?
cards.back: If a firm frequently rely on sales promotion, it may give the impression that it is unable to manage its sales
cards.quote: If a firm frequently rely on sales promotion, it may give the impression that it is unable to manage its sales

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Sales promotion limitation: 'Spoils Product Image'. What does it mean?
cards.back: Use of sales promotion tools may affect the image of a product.
cards.quote: Use of sales promotion tools may affect the image of a product.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Sales promotion activity: what is a rebate?
cards.back: Rebate: Offering products at special prices, to clear off excess inventory.
cards.quote: Rebate: Offering products at special prices, to clear off excess inventory.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Sales promotion activity: what is a discount?
cards.back: Discount: Offering products at less than list price.
cards.quote: Discount: Offering products at less than list price.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Sales promotion activity: what are refunds?
cards.back: Refunds: refunding a part of price paid by customer on some proof of purchase, say on return of empty foils or wrapper.
cards.quote: Refunds: refunding a part of price paid by customer on some proof of purchase, say on return of empty foils or wrapper.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Sales promotion activity: what is sampling?
cards.back: Sampling: Offer of free sample of a product, say a detergent powder or tooth paste to potential customers at the time of launch of a new brand.
cards.quote: Sampling: Offer of free sample of a product, say a detergent powder or tooth paste to potential customers at the time of launch of a new brand.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define publicity.
cards.back: Publicity is similar to advertising, in the sense that it is a non-personal form of communication. However, as against advertising it is a non-paid form of communication.
cards.quote: Publicity is similar to advertising, in the sense that it is a non-personal form of communication. However, as against advertising it is a non-paid form of communication.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What do public relations involve?
cards.back: public relations involve a variety of programmes designed to promote or protect a company's image and its individual products in the eyes of the public.
cards.quote: public relations involve a variety of programmes designed to promote or protect a company's image and its individual products in the eyes of the public.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the two important features of publicity.
cards.back:
(i) Publicity is an unpaid form of communication. It does not involve any direct expenditure by the marketing firm; and
(ii) There is no identified sponsor for the communication as the message goes as a news item.
cards.quote: (i) Publicity is an unpaid form of communication. It does not involve any direct expenditure by the marketing firm; and (ii) There is no identified sponsor for the communication as the message goes as a news item.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Public relations department: name four functions besides publicity.
cards.back:
2. Press release
3. Corporate communication
4. Lobbying
5. Counselling
cards.quote: 2. Press release: Information about the organisation needs to be presented in a positive manner in the press. Generating news requires skill in developing and researching a story and getting the media to accept press releases is a difficult task. The public relations department is in contact with the media to present true facts and a correct picture about the company. Otherwise news can get distorted if taken from other sources. 3. Corporate communication: The image of the organisation needs to be promoted through communicating with the public and the employees within the organisation. This is usually done with the help of newsletter, annual reports, brochures, articles and audio-visual materials. Companies rely on these materials to reach and influence their target markets. Speeches by the company's executives at a meeting of trade associations or trade fairs can really boost the company's image. even interviews with TV channels and responding to queries from the media go a long way in promoting public relations. 4. Lobbying: The organisation has to deal with government officials and different ministers in charge of corporate affairs, industry, finance with respect to policies relating to business and the economy. The government also seeks to maintain a healthy relationship with associations of commerce and industry and solicits the opinion of major stakeholders while formulating industrial, telecom, taxation policies, etc. The public relations department then has to be really proactive in promoting or decoding regulations that affect them. 5. Counselling: The public relations department advises the management on general issues which affect the public and the position the company would like to the take on a particular issue. The company can build goodwill by contributing money and time to certain causes like environment, wildlife, children's rights, education, etc. Such cause-related activities help in promoting public relations and building goodwill.

cards.back: Personal selling is a personal form of communication.
cards.quote: Personal selling is a personal form of communication.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Advertising vs personal selling: advertising lacks direct feedback. What feedback does personal selling give?
cards.back: Personal selling provides direct and immediate feed back. Sales persons come to know about the customers’ reactions immediately.

cards.front: Advertising vs personal selling: advertising suits many ultimate consumers. Who is personal selling more helpful for?
cards.back: Personal selling is more helpful in selling products to the industrial buyers or to imtermediaries such as dealers and retailers who are relatively few in numbers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the marketing objectives good public relations helps to achieve.
cards.back:
(a) Building awareness
(b) Building credibility
(c) Stimulates sales force
(d) Lowers promotion costs
cards.quote: (a) Building awareness: Public relations department can place stories and dramatise the product in the media. This will build marketplace excitement before the product reaches the market or media advertising takes place. This usually creates a favourable impression on the target customer. (b) Building credibility: If news about a product comes in the media whether print or electronic it always lends credibility and people believe in the product since it is in the news. (c) Stimulates sales force: It becomes easier for the sales force to deal with the retailers and convince dealers if they have already heard about the product in the news before it is launched. Retailers and dealers also feel it is easier to sell the product to the ultimate consumer. (d) Lowers promotion costs: Maintaining good public relations costs much less than advertising and direct mail. However, it requires a lot of communication and interpersonal skills to convince the media to give space or time for the organisation and its product.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: State the role of marketing (NCERT summary).
cards.back: By adopting marketing orientation, an organisation whether profit making or non-profit making, can achieve its goals in the most effective manner. Also marketing acts as a catalyst in the economic development of a country and helps in raising the standards of living of people.

Convenience Product
Shopping Products

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the functions of packaging (NCERT summary).
cards.back:
Product identification
Product protection
Facilitating the use of the product
Promotion of goods and services
cards.quote: Some of the important functions, include Product identification; Product protection; Facilitating the use of the product and Promotion of goods and services.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five functions performed by a label.
cards.back:
Describe the Product and specify its contents
Identification of the Product or brand
Grading of Products
Helps in Promotion of Products
Providing Information Required by Law
cards.quote: The various functions performed by a label are as follows: 1. Describe the Product and specify its contents: Let us look at some of the labels of the products used by us in our day to day life. The label on the package of a local tea company describes the company as ‘Mohini Tea Company, an ISO 9001:200C Certified Company’; a popular brand of Prickly Heat Powder, describes how the product provides relief from prickly heat and controls bacterial growth and infection, giving caution forbidding its application on cuts and wounds. Package of fast food products like ready to eat Dosa, Idli or Noodles, describe the procedure of cooking these products; the Package of a toothpaste brand lists the ‘Ten Teeth and Gum Problems’, which the product claims to fight with its ‘Complete Germicheck Formula’; the Package of a brand of Coconut Oil describes the product as pure coconut oil with Heena, Amla, Lemon and specifies how these are good for Hair. Thus, one of the most important functions of labels is to describe the product, its usage, cautions in use, etc. and specify its contents. 2. Identification of the Product or brand: The other important function performed by labels is to help in identifying the product or brand. For example, the brand name of any product, say Biscuits or Potato Chips imprinted on its package helps us to identify, from number of packages, which one is our favourite brand. Other common identification information provided by the labels include name and address of the manufacturer, net weight when packed, manufacturing date, maximum retail price and Batch number. 3. Grading of Products: Another important function performed by labels is to help grading the products into different categories. Sometimes marketers assign different grades to indicate different features or quality of the product. For example, a popular brand of Hair Conditioners comes in different categories for different hair, say for ‘normal hair’ and for other categories. Different type of tea is sold by some brands under Yellow, red and Green Label categories. 4. Helps in Promotion of Products: An important function of label is to aid in promotion of the products. A carefully designed label can attract attention and give reason to purchase. We see many product labels providing promotional messages for example, the pack of a popular Amla Hair Oil states, ‘Baalon mein Dum, Life mein Fun’. The label on the package of a brand of Detergent Powder says, ‘keep cloth look good and your machine in top condition’. Labels play important role in sales promotional schemes launched by companies. For example the label on the package of a Shaving Cream mentions, ‘40% Extra Free’ or package of a toothpaste mentioning, ‘Free Toothbrush Inside’, or ‘Save `15’. 5. Providing Information Required by Law: Another important function of labeling is to provide information required by law.

cards.quote: For products requiring long-term storage (such as agricultural products) the warehouses are located near production sites. This helps in minimising the charges on transportation of the goods.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Which marketing function covers after sales services, complaint handling, credit, maintenance and consumer information?
cards.back: A very important function of the marketing management relates to developing customer support services such as after sales services, handling customer complaints and adjustments, procuring credit services, maintenance services, technical services and consumer information.
cards.quote: A very important function of the marketing management relates to developing customer support services such as after sales services, handling customer complaints and adjustments, procuring credit services, maintenance services, technical services and consumer information.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define management (Harold Koontz and Heinz Weihrich).
cards.back: Management is the process of designing and maintaining an environment in which individuals, working together in groups, efficiently accomplish selected aims.
cards.quote: Management is the process of designing and maintaining an environment in which individuals, working together in groups, efficiently accomplish selected aims.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define management (Robert L. Trewelly and M. Gene Newport).
cards.back: Management is defined as the process of planning, organising, actuating and controlling an organisation's operations in order to achieve coordination of the human and material resources essential in the effective and efficient attainment of objectives.
cards.quote: Management is defined as the process of planning, organising, actuating and controlling an organisation's operations in order to achieve coordination of the human and material resources essential in the effective and efficient attainment of objectives.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define management (Kreitner).
cards.back: Management is the process of working with and through others to effectively achieve organisational objectives by efficiently using limited resources in the changing environment.
cards.quote: Management is the process of working with and through others to effectively achieve organisational objectives by efficiently using limited resources in the changing environment.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define management as a process of getting things done.
cards.back: Management, has therefore, been defined as a process of getting things done with the aim of achieving goals effectively and efficiently.
cards.quote: Management, has therefore, been defined as a process of getting things done with the aim of achieving goals effectively and efficiently.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does 'process' mean in the definition of management?
cards.back: Process in the definition means the primary functions or activities that management performs to get things done. These functions are planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling which we will discuss later in the chapter and the book.
cards.quote: Process in the definition means the primary functions or activities that management performs to get things done. These functions are planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling which we will discuss later in the chapter and the book.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is effectiveness in management?
cards.back: Effectiveness in management is concerned with doing the right task, completing activities and achieving goals. In other words, it is concerned with the end result.
cards.quote: Effectiveness in management is concerned with doing the right task, completing activities and achieving goals. In other words, it is concerned with the end result.
cards.note: Effectiveness is about the result: the right task done and goals reached.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is efficiency in management?
cards.back: Efficiency means doing the task correctly and with minimum cost.
cards.quote: Efficiency means doing the task correctly and with minimum cost.
cards.note: Efficiency is about the means: benefits (outputs) compared with resources used (inputs).

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: If by using less resources (i.e., the inputs) more benefits are derived (i.e., the outputs) then ____ has increased.
cards.back: If by using less resources (i.e., the inputs) more benefits are derived (i.e., the outputs) then efficiency has increased.
cards.quote: If by using less resources (i.e., the inputs) more benefits are derived (i.e., the outputs) then efficiency has increased.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the input resources needed to do a task.
cards.back:
money
materials
equipment
persons required to do a particular task
cards.quote: Input resources are money, materials, equipment and persons required to do a particular task.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: A 5000-unit target is met on double shifts (power failure) at a higher production cost. Effective, efficient or both?
cards.back:
Effective but not so efficient
The manager is able to produce 5000 units but at a higher production cost. In this case, the manager was effective but not so efficient, since for the same output, more inputs (labour cost, electricity costs) were used.
cards.quote: The manager is able to produce 5000 units but at a higher production cost. In this case, the manager was effective but not so efficient, since for the same output, more inputs (labour cost, electricity costs) were used.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: A business cuts costs with fewer resources but misses target production; goods do not reach the market. Effective or efficient?
cards.back: This is a case of being efficient but not effective since the goods did not reach the market.
cards.quote: This is a case of being efficient but not effective since the goods did not reach the market.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is poor management due to, according to NCERT?
cards.back: Poor management is due to both inefficiency and ineffectiveness.
cards.quote: Poor management is due to both inefficiency and ineffectiveness.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is a ____ process: An organisation has a set of basic goals which are the basic reason for its existence.
cards.back: Management is a goal-oriented process: An organisation has a set of basic goals which are the basic reason for its existence.
cards.quote: Management is a goal-oriented process: An organisation has a set of basic goals which are the basic reason for its existence.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is ____: The activities involved in managing an enterprise are common to all organisations whether economic, social or political.
cards.back: Management is all pervasive: The activities involved in managing an enterprise are common to all organisations whether economic, social or political.
cards.quote: Management is all pervasive: The activities involved in managing an enterprise are common to all organisations whether economic, social or political.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Petrol pump, hospital or school: all need managing. Which characteristic of management is this?
cards.back: Management is all pervasive: The activities involved in managing an enterprise are common to all organisations whether economic, social or political. A petrol pump needs to be managed as much as a hospital or a school.
cards.quote: Management is all pervasive: The activities involved in managing an enterprise are common to all organisations whether economic, social or political. A petrol pump needs to be managed as much as a hospital or a school.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are the two dimensions of managing people?
cards.back:
dealing with employees as individuals with diverse needs and behavior
dealing with individuals as a group of people
cards.quote: (i) it implies dealing with employees as individuals with diverse needs and behavior; (ii) it also means dealing with individuals as a group of people.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is a group activity. Why does every member join the organisation, and what do they work towards?
cards.back:
Different purposes for joining, one common goal
Every member of the group has a different purpose for joining the organisation but as members of the organisation they work towards fulfilling the common organisational goal. This requires team work and coordination of individual effort in a common direction.
cards.quote: Every member of the group has a different purpose for joining the organisation but as members of the organisation they work towards fulfilling the common organisational goal. This requires team work and coordination of individual effort in a common direction.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is a continuous process: who performs its five functions, and when?
cards.back: The process of management is a series of continuous, composite, but separate functions (planning, organising, directing, staffing and controlling). These functions are simultaneously performed by all managers all the time.
cards.quote: The process of management is a series of continuous, composite, but separate functions (planning, organising, directing, staffing and controlling). These functions are simultaneously performed by all managers all the time.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is a ____: An organisation is a collection of diverse individuals with different needs.
cards.back: Management is a group activity: An organisation is a collection of diverse individuals with different needs.
cards.quote: Management is a group activity: An organisation is a collection of diverse individuals with different needs.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is a ____ function and has to adapt itself to the changing environment.
cards.back: Management is a dynamic function and has to adapt itself to the changing environment.
cards.quote: Management is a dynamic function and has to adapt itself to the changing environment.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: McDonalds changed its menu to survive in the Indian market. Which feature of management is this?
cards.back:
Management is a dynamic function
In order to be successful, an organisation must change itself and its goals according to the needs of the environment. You probably know that McDonalds, the fast food giant made major changes in its menu to be able to survive in the Indian market.
cards.quote: In order to be successful, an organisation must change itself and its goals according to the needs of the environment. You probably know that McDonalds, the fast food giant made major changes in its menu to be able to survive in the Indian market.
cards.note: This is management as a dynamic function.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is an ____ force that cannot be seen but its presence can be felt in the way the organisation functions.
cards.back: Management is an intangible force that cannot be seen but its presence can be felt in the way the organisation functions.
cards.quote: Management is an intangible force that cannot be seen but its presence can be felt in the way the organisation functions.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Types of objectives of management.
cards.back:
organisational objectives
social objectives
personal or individual objectives
cards.quote: Objectives can be classified into organisational objectives, social objectives and personal or individual objectives.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the three economic objectives of a business.
cards.back:
Survival
Profit
Growth
cards.quote: i.e., to fulfill the economic objectives of a business. These are survival, profit and growth.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are social objectives of management?
cards.back: Social objectives: It involves the creation of benefit for society. As a part of society, every organisation whether it is business or non-business, has a social obligation to fulfill.
cards.quote: Social objectives: It involves the creation of benefit for society. As a part of society, every organisation whether it is business or non-business, has a social obligation to fulfill.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are personnel objectives of management?
cards.back: Personnel objectives: Organisations are made up of people who have different personalities, backgrounds, experiences and objectives. They all become part of the organisation to satisfy their diverse needs.
cards.quote: Personnel objectives: Organisations are made up of people who have different personalities, backgrounds, experiences and objectives. They all become part of the organisation to satisfy their diverse needs.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Types of needs that personnel objectives aim to satisfy.
cards.back:
financial needs such as competitive salaries and perks
social needs such as peer recognition
higher level needs such as personal growth and development
cards.quote: These vary from financial needs such as competitive salaries and perks, social needs such as peer recognition and higher level needs such as personal growth and development.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five reasons why management is important.
cards.back:
helps in achieving group goals
increases efficiency
creates a dynamic organisation
helps achieve personal objectives
contributes to the development of society
cards.quote: Management is important because it helps in achieving group goals, increases efficiency, creates a dynamic organisation, helps achieve personal objectives and contributes to the development of society.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is art?
cards.back: Art is the skillful and personal application of existing knowledge to achieve desired results.
cards.quote: Art is the skillful and personal application of existing knowledge to achieve desired results.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the basic features of an art.
cards.back:
Existence of theoretical knowledge
Personalised application
Based on practice and creativity
cards.quote: The basic features of an art are as follows: (i) Existence of theoretical knowledge: Art presupposes the existence of certain theoretical knowledge. Experts in their respective areas have derived certain basic principles which are applicable to a particular form of art. For example, literature on dancing, public speaking, acting or music is widely recognised. (ii) Personalised application: The use of this basic knowledge varies from individual to individual. Art, therefore, is a very personalised concept. For example, two dancers, two speakers, two actors, or two writers will always differ in demonstrating their art. (iii) Based on practice and creativity

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is science?
cards.back: Science is a systematised body of knowledge that explains certain general truths or the operation of general laws.
cards.quote: Science is a systematised body of knowledge that explains certain general truths or the operation of general laws.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the basic features of science.
cards.back:
Systematised body of knowledge
Principles based on experimentation
Universal validity
cards.quote: (i) Systematised body of knowledge: Science is a systematic body of knowledge. Its principles are based on a cause and effect relationship. For example, the phenomenon of an apple falling from a tree towards the ground is explained by the law of gravity. (ii) Principles based on experimentation: Scientific principles are first developed through observation and then tested through repeated experimentation under controlled conditions.
