(iii) Universal validity: Scientific principles have universal validity and application.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Why is management called an inexact science?
cards.back: Since management deals with human beings and human behaviour, the outcomes of these experiments are not capable of being accurately predicted or replicated.
cards.quote: since management deals with human beings and human behaviour, the outcomes of these experiments are not capable of being accurately predicted or replicated. Therefore, management can be called an inexact science.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Who gave scientific management principles, and who gave functional management principles?
cards.back: For example, scientific management principles by F.W. Taylor and Functional Management principles by Henri Fayol which you will study in the next chapter.
cards.quote: For example, scientific management principles by F.W. Taylor and Functional Management principles by Henri Fayol which you will study in the next chapter.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Which part of management is an art and which part is science?
cards.back: The practice of management is an art. However, managers can work better if their practice is based on the principles of management. These principles constitute the science of management.
cards.quote: The practice of management is an art. However, managers can work better if their practice is based on the principles of management. These principles constitute the science of management.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management as an art and a science are therefore not ____, but ____ each other.
cards.back: Management as an art and a science are therefore not mutually exclusive, but complement each other.
cards.quote: Management as an art and a science are therefore not mutually exclusive, but complement each other.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the characteristics of a profession.
cards.back:
Well-defined body of knowledge
Restricted entry
Professional association
Ethical code of conduct
Service motive
cards.quote: A profession has the following characteristics: (i) Well-defined body of knowledge: All professions are based on a well-defined body of knowledge that can be acquired through instruction. (ii) Restricted entry: The entry to a profession is restricted through an examination or through acquiring an educational degree. For example, to become a chartered accountant in India a candidate has to clear a specified examination conducted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. (iii) Professional association: All professions are affiliated to a professional association which regulates entry, grants certificate of practice and formulates and enforces a code of conduct. To be able to practice in India lawyers have to become members of the Bar Council which regulates and controls their activities. (iv) Ethical code of conduct: All professions are bound by a code of conduct which guides the behaviour of its members. All doctors, for example, take the oath of ethical practice at the time they enter the profession. (v) Service motive: The basic motive of a profession is to serve their client’s interests by rendering dedicated and committed service. The task of a lawyer is to ensure that his client gets justice.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: A candidate must clear an ICAI examination to become a chartered accountant. Which feature of a profession?
cards.back: Restricted entry: The entry to a profession is restricted through an examination or through acquiring an educational degree. For example, to become a chartered accountant in India a candidate has to clear a specified examination conducted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.
cards.quote: Restricted entry: The entry to a profession is restricted through an examination or through acquiring an educational degree. For example, to become a chartered accountant in India a candidate has to clear a specified examination conducted by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Lawyers are affiliated to the Bar Council, which regulates and controls their activities. Which feature of a profession?
cards.back: Professional association: All professions are affiliated to a professional association which regulates entry, grants certificate of practice and formulates and enforces a code of conduct. To be able to practice in India lawyers have to become members of the Bar Council which regulates and controls their activities.
cards.quote: Professional association: All professions are affiliated to a professional association which regulates entry, grants certificate of practice and formulates and enforces a code of conduct. To be able to practice in India lawyers have to become members of the Bar Council which regulates and controls their activities.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Does management meet the exact criteria of a profession?
cards.back: Management does not meet the exact criteria of a profession. However, it does have some of the features of a profession.
cards.quote: Management does not meet the exact criteria of a profession. However, it does have some of the features of a profession

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Levels of management and what each focuses on.
cards.back:
The top management focuses on determination of objectives and policies
middle management attempts to achieve these objectives through the effort of other managers
supervisory or operational management directly oversees the efforts of the workforce
cards.quote: Management is considered a three-tier activity. The top management focuses on determination of objectives and policies, middle management attempts to achieve these objectives through the effort of other managers and supervisory or operational management directly oversees the efforts of the workforce.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Who constitute top management?
cards.back: Top Management: They consist of the senior-most executives of the organisation by whatever name they are called. They are usually referred to as the chairman, the chief executive officer, chief operating officer, president and vice-president.
cards.quote: Top Management: They consist of the senior-most executives of the organisation by whatever name they are called. They are usually referred to as the chairman, the chief executive officer, chief operating officer, president and vice-president.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is the basic task of top management?
cards.back: To integrate diverse elements and coordinate the activities of different departments according to the overall objectives of the organisation.
cards.quote: Their basic task is to integrate diverse elements and coordinate the activities of different departments according to the overall objectives of the organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is middle management?
cards.back: Middle Management: is the link between top and lower level managers. They are subordinate to top managers and superior to the first line managers.
cards.quote: Middle Management: is the link between top and lower level managers. They are subordinate to top managers and superior to the first line managers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What must middle managers do to carry out top management's plans?
cards.back:
interpret the policies framed by top management
ensure that their department has the necessary personnel
assign necessary duties and responsibilities to them
motivate them to achieve desired objectives
co-operate with other departments for smooth functioning
cards.quote: Their main task is to carry out the plans formulated by the top managers. For this they need to: (i) interpret the policies framed by top management, (ii) ensure that their department has the necessary personnel, (iii) assign necessary duties and responsibilities to them, (iv) motivate them to achieve desired objectives, and (v) cooperate with other departments for smooth functioning

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is supervisory (operational) management?
cards.back: Supervisory or Operational Management: Foremen and supervisors comprise the lower level in the hierarchy of the organisation. Supervisors directly oversee the efforts of the workforce.
cards.quote: Supervisory or Operational Management: Foremen and supervisors comprise the lower level in the hierarchy of the organisation. Supervisors directly oversee the efforts of the workforce.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is organising?
cards.back: Organising is the management function of assigning duties, grouping tasks, establishing authority and allocating resources required to carry out a specific plan.
cards.quote: Organising is the management function of assigning duties, grouping tasks, establishing authority and allocating resources required to carry out a specific plan.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is staffing?
cards.back: Staffing simply stated, is finding the right people for the right job.
cards.quote: Staffing simply stated, is finding the right people for the right job.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is directing?
cards.back: Directing involves leading, influencing and motivating employees to perform the tasks assigned to them.
cards.quote: Directing involves leading, influencing and motivating employees to perform the tasks assigned to them.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is controlling?
cards.back: Controlling is the management function of monitoring organisational performance towards the attainment of organisational goals.
cards.quote: Controlling is the management function of monitoring organisational performance towards the attainment of organisational goals.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Steps in controlling, in order.
cards.back: The task of controlling involves establishing standards of performance, measuring current performance, comparing this with established standards and taking corrective action where any deviation is found.
cards.quote: The task of controlling involves establishing standards of performance, measuring current performance, comparing this with established standards and taking corrective action where any deviation is found.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The order in which managerial functions are usually discussed.
cards.back:
first plans
then organises
puts staff in position
then directs
and finally controls
cards.quote: The various functions of a manager are usually discussed in the order given above, suggesting that a manager first plans, then organises, puts staff in position, then directs, and finally controls.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is coordination?
cards.back: The process by which a manager synchronises the activities of different departments is known as coordination.
cards.quote: The process by which a manager synchronises the activities of different departments is known as coordination.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: ____ is the force that binds all the other functions of management.
cards.back: Coordination is the force that binds all the other functions of management.
cards.quote: Coordination is the force that binds all the other functions of management.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: ____, therefore, is not a separate function of management, but its very essence.
cards.back: Coordination, therefore, is not a separate function of management, but its very essence.
cards.quote: Coordination, therefore, is not a separate function of management, but its very essence.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define coordination (E.F.L. Brech).
cards.back: Coordination is balancing and keeping together the team by ensuring suitable allocation of tasks to the various members and seeing that the tasks are performed with harmony among the members themselves.
cards.quote: Coordination is balancing and keeping together the team by ensuring suitable allocation of tasks to the various members and seeing that the tasks are performed with harmony among the members themselves.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define coordination (McFarland).
cards.back: Coordination is the process whereby an executive develops an orderly pattern of group efforts among his subordinates and secures unity of action in the pursuit of common purpose.
cards.quote: Coordination is the process whereby an executive develops an orderly pattern of group efforts among his subordinates and secures unity of action in the pursuit of common purpose.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define coordination (Theo Haimann).
cards.back: Coordination is the orderly synchronising of efforts of subordinates to provide proper amount, timing and quality of execution so that their united efforts lead to the stated objectives, namely, the common purpose of the enterprise.
cards.quote: Coordination is the orderly synchronising of efforts of subordinates to provide proper amount, timing and quality of execution so that their united efforts lead to the stated objectives, namely, the common purpose of the enterprise.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Why is coordination important? What does it integrate?
cards.back: Coordination is important as it integrates the efforts of individuals, departments and specialists.
cards.quote: Coordination is important as it integrates the efforts of individuals, departments and specialists.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does coordination unify into purposeful work activity?
cards.back: Coordination unifies unrelated or diverse interests into purposeful work activity. It gives a common focus to group effort to ensure that performance is as it was planned and scheduled.
cards.quote: Coordination unifies unrelated or diverse interests into purposeful work activity. It gives a common focus to group effort to ensure that performance is as it was planned and scheduled.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Coordination ensures unity of action. What is its purpose?
cards.back:
Coordination ensures unity of action
The purpose of coordination is to secure unity of action in the realisation of a common purpose.
cards.quote: The purpose of coordination is to secure unity of action in the realisation of a common purpose.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Coordination is a continuous process. When does it begin and till where does it continue?
cards.back:
Coordination is a continuous process
Coordination is not a one-time function but a continuous process. It begins at the planning stage and continues till controlling.
cards.quote: Coordination is not a one-time function but a continuous process. It begins at the planning stage and continues till controlling.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Coordination is an all pervasive function. Where is it required, and why?
cards.back:
Coordination is an all pervasive function
Coordination is required at all levels of management due to the interdependent nature of activities of various departments.
cards.quote: Coordination is required at all levels of management due to the interdependent nature of activities of various departments.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is management (chapter summary)?
cards.back: Management is the process of planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling the enterprise resources efficiently and effectively for achieving the goals of the organisation.
cards.quote: Management is the process of planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling the enterprise resources efficiently and effectively for achieving the goals of the organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the interrelated functions performed by all managers.
cards.back:
Planning
Organising
Staffing
Directing
Controlling
cards.quote: All managers perform the following interrelated functions: Planning, Organising, Staffing, Directing and Controlling.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management is a combination of an organised body of knowledge (____) and its skillful application (____).
cards.back: Management is a combination of an organised body of knowledge (science) and its skillful application (art).
cards.quote: Management is a combination of an organised body of knowledge (science) and its skillful application (art).

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is coordination (chapter summary)?
cards.back: Coordination is the essence of management. It is the process of achieving unity of action among interdependent activities and departments of an organisation.
cards.quote: Coordination is the essence of management. It is the process of achieving unity of action among interdependent activities and departments of an organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define organising.
cards.back: Organising can be defined as a process that initiates implementation of plans by clarifying jobs and working relationships and effectively deploying resources for attainment of identified and desired results (goals).
cards.quote: Organising can be defined as a process that initiates implementation of plans by clarifying jobs and working relationships and effectively deploying resources for attainment of identified and desired results (goals).

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define organising (Louis Allen).
cards.back: Organising is the process of identifying and grouping the work to be performed, defining and delegating responsibility and authority, and establishing relationships for the purpose of enabling people to work most effectively together in accomplishing objectives.
cards.quote: Organising is the process of identifying and grouping the work to be performed, defining and delegating responsibility and authority, and establishing relationships for the purpose of enabling people to work most effectively together in accomplishing objectives.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define organising (Theo Haimman).
cards.back: Organising is the process of defining and grouping the activities of the enterprise and establishing authority relationships among them.
cards.quote: Organising is the process of defining and grouping the activities of the enterprise and establishing authority relationships among them.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four steps in the process of organising, in order.
cards.back:
Identification and division of work
Departmentalisation
Assignment of Duties
Establishing reporting relationships
cards.quote: (a) Identification and division of work (b) Departmentalisation (c) Assignment of Duties (d) Establishing reporting relationships

source.section: Steps in the Process of Organising

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The first step in the process of organising involves ____ that has to be done in accordance with previously determined plans.
cards.back: The first step in the process of organising involves identifying and dividing the work that has to be done in accordance with previously determined plans.
cards.quote: The first step in the process of organising involves identifying and dividing the work that has to be done in accordance with previously determined plans.

source.section: Steps in the Process of Organising

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Once work has been divided into small and manageable activities then those activities which are ____ are grouped together.
cards.back: Once work has been divided into small and manageable activities then those activities which are similar in nature are grouped together.
cards.quote: Once work has been divided into small and manageable activities then those activities which are similar in nature are grouped together.

source.section: Steps in the Process of Organising

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the six points on the importance of organising (NCERT chapter summary).
cards.back:
division of work
clarity in reporting relationships
optimum utilization of resources
growth
better administration
greater creativity
cards.quote: Importance: Organising is considered important because it leads to division of work, clarity in reporting relationships, optimum utilization of resources, growth, better administration and greater creativity.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Organising leads to the proper usage of all ____.
cards.back: Organising leads to the proper usage of all material, financial and human resources.
cards.quote: Organising leads to the proper usage of all material, financial and human resources.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Organisation structure is the outcome of which process?
cards.back:
The organising process
Organisation structure is the outcome of the organising process.
cards.quote: Organisation structure is the outcome of the organising process.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define organisation structure.
cards.back: The organisation structure can be defined as the framework within which managerial and operating tasks are performed.
cards.quote: The organisation structure can be defined as the framework within which managerial and operating tasks are performed.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The organisation structure of a firm is shown in an ____.
cards.back: The organisation structure of a firm is shown in an organisation chart.
cards.quote: The organisation structure of a firm is shown in an organisation chart.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is span of management?
cards.back: Span of management refers to the number of subordinates that can be effectively managed by a superior.
cards.quote: Span of management refers to the number of subordinates that can be effectively managed by a superior.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Who said that "organisation structure is an indispensable means"?
cards.back: Peter Drucker emphasises on the importance of having an appropriate organisation structure when he says, "organisation structure is an indispensable means; and the wrong structure will seriously impair business performance and even destroy it."
cards.quote: Peter Drucker emphasises on the importance of having an appropriate organisation structure when he says, “organisation structure is an indispensable means; and the wrong structure will seriously impair business performance and even destroy it.”

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Types of organisation structures.
cards.back:
Functional structure
Divisional structure
cards.quote: (i) Functional structure and (ii) Divisional structure

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a functional structure?
cards.back: Thus, a functional structure is an organisational design that groups similar or related jobs together.
cards.quote: Thus, a functional structure is an organisational design that groups similar or related jobs together.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the advantages of the functional structure.
cards.back:
specialisation
better control
managerial efficiency
ease in training employees
cards.quote: The advantages of such a structure are specialisation, better control, managerial efficiency and ease in training employees.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the disadvantages of the functional structure.
cards.back:
functional empires
conflict of interest
inflexibility
restriction in managerial development
cards.quote: The disadvantages are functional empires, conflict of interest, inflexibility, and restriction in managerial development.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Functional structure: emphasis on a functional head's objectives over enterprise objectives may lead to what?
cards.back: A functional structure places less emphasis on overall enterprise objectives than the objectives pursued by a functional head. Such practices may lead to functional empires wherein the importance of a particular function may be overemphasised.
cards.quote: A functional structure places less emphasis on overall enterprise objectives than the objectives pursued by a functional head. Such practices may lead to functional empires wherein the importance of a particular function may be overemphasised.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: When is the functional structure most suitable, according to NCERT?
cards.back:
Large size, diversified activities, high specialisation
Suitability: It is most suitable when the size of the organisation is large, has a diversified activities and operations require a high degree of specialisation.
cards.quote: Suitability: It is most suitable when the size of the organisation is large, has a diversified activities and operations require a high degree of specialisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a divisional structure?
cards.back: In a divisional structure, the organisation structure comprises of separate business units or divisions.
cards.quote: In a divisional structure, the organisation structure comprises of separate business units or divisions.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Generally, manpower is grouped on the basis of ____ manufactured.
cards.back: Generally, manpower is grouped on the basis of different products manufactured.
cards.quote: Generally, manpower is grouped on the basis of different products manufactured.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Further, each division works as a ____ where the divisional head is responsible for the profit or loss of his division.
cards.back: Further, each division works as a profit center where the divisional head is responsible for the profit or loss of his division.
cards.quote: Further, each division works as a profit center where the divisional head is responsible for the profit or loss of his division.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the advantages of the divisional structure.
cards.back:
integration
product specialisation
greater accountability
flexibility
better coordination
more initiative
cards.quote: The advantages are integration, product specialisation, greater accountability, flexibility, better coordination and more initiative.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the disadvantages of the divisional structure.
cards.back:
departmental conflicts
costly process
ignoring of organisational interests
increase in requirements of general managers
cards.quote: The disadvantages are departmental conflicts, costly process, ignoring of organisational interests, increase in requirements of general managers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Divisional structure is suitable for those business enterprises where a ____ are manufactured using different productive resources.
cards.back: Divisional structure is suitable for those business enterprises where a large variety of products are manufactured using different productive resources.
cards.quote: Divisional structure is suitable for those business enterprises where a large variety of products are manufactured using different productive resources.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Functional vs divisional structure: the difference on formation (functional first, divisional second).
cards.back:
Formation is based on functions
Formation is based on product lines and is supported by functions.
cards.quote: Formation Formation is based on functions Formation is based on product lines and is supported by functions.

source.section: Comparative view: Functional and Divisional Structure

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Functional vs divisional structure: the difference on specialisation (functional first, divisional second).
cards.back:
Functional specialisation.
Product specialisation.
cards.quote: Specialisation Functional specialisation. Product specialisation.

source.section: Comparative view: Functional and Divisional Structure

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Functional vs divisional structure: the difference on responsibility (functional first, divisional second).
cards.back:
Difficult to fix on a department.
Easy to fix responsiblity for performance.
cards.quote: Responsibility Difficult to fix on a department. Easy to fix responsiblity for performance.

source.section: Comparative view: Functional and Divisional Structure

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Functional vs divisional structure: the difference on managerial development (functional first, divisional second).
cards.back:
Difficult, as each functional manager has to report to the top management.
Easier, autonomy as well as the chance to perform multiple functions helps in managerial development.
cards.quote: Difficult, as each functional manager has to report to the top management. Easier, autonomy as well as the chance to perform multiple functions helps in managerial development.

source.section: Comparative view: Functional and Divisional Structure

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Functional vs divisional structure: the difference on cost (functional first, divisional second).
cards.back:
Functions are not duplicated hence economical
Duplication of resources in various departments, hence costly.
cards.quote: Cost Functions are not duplicated hence economical Duplication of resources in various departments, hence costly.

source.section: Comparative view: Functional and Divisional Structure

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Functional vs divisional structure: the difference on coordination (functional first, divisional second).
cards.back:
Difficult for a multiproduct company.
Easy, because all functions related to a particular product are integrated in one department.
cards.quote: Coordination Difficult for a multi–product company. Easy, because all functions related to a particular product are integrated in one department.

source.section: Comparative view: Functional and Divisional Structure

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a formal organisation?
cards.back: Formal organisation refers to the organisation structure which is designed by the management to accomplish a particular task.
cards.quote: Formal organisation refers to the organisation structure which is designed by the management to accomplish a particular task.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define formal organisation (Louis Allen).
cards.back: The formal organisation is a system of well-defined jobs, each bearing a definite measure of authority, responsibility and accountability.
cards.quote: The formal organisation is a system of well-defined jobs, each bearing a definite measure of authority, responsibility and accountability.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define formal organisation (Chester Barnard).
cards.back: Formal organisation is a system of consciously coordinated activities of two or more persons toward a common objective.
cards.quote: Formal organisation is a system of consciously coordinated activities of two or more persons toward a common objective.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the features of the formal organisation.
cards.back:
It specifies the relationships among various job positions and the nature of their inter-relationship.
It is a means to achieve the objectives specified in the plans, as it lays down rules and procedures essential for their achievement.
Efforts of various departments are coordinated, interlinked and integrated through the formal organisation.
It is deliberately designed by the top management to facilitate the smooth functioning of the organisation.
It places more emphasis on work to be performed than interpersonal relationships among the employees.
cards.quote: (a) It specifies the relationships among various job positions and the nature of their inter-relationship. This clarifies who has to report to whom. (b) It is a means to achieve the objectives specified in the plans, as it lays down rules and procedures essential for their achievement. (c) Efforts of various departments are coordinated, interlinked and integrated through the formal organisation. (d) It is deliberately designed by the top management to facilitate the smooth functioning of the organisation. (e) It places more emphasis on work to be performed than interpersonal relationships among the employees.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the advantages of the formal organisation.
cards.back:
fixation of responsibility
clarity of roles
unity of command
effective accomplishment of goals
cards.quote: Its advantages are fixation of responsibility, clarity of roles, unity of command and effective accomplishment of goals.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the limitations of the formal organisation.
cards.back:
procedural delays
inadequate recognition of creativity
limited in scope
cards.quote: Its disadvantages are procedural delays, inadequate recognition of creativity, limited in scope.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is an informal organisation?
cards.back: Interaction among people at work gives rise to a ‘network of social relationships among employees’ called the informal organisation.
cards.quote: Interaction among people at work gives rise to a ‘network of social relationships among employees’ called the informal organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define informal organisation (Chester Barnard).
cards.back: An informal organisation is an aggregate of interpersonal relationships without any conscious purpose but which may contribute to joint results.
cards.quote: An informal organisation is an aggregate of interpersonal relationships without any conscious purpose but which may contribute to joint results.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define informal organisation (Keith Davis).
cards.back: Informal organisation is a network of personal and social relations not established or required by the formal organisation but arising spontaneously as people associate with one another.
cards.quote: Informal organisation is a network of personal and social relations not established or required by the formal organisation but arising spontaneously as people associate with one another.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the features of the informal organisation.
cards.back:
An informal organisation originates from within the formal organisation as a result of personal interaction among employees.
The standards of behaviour evolve from group norms rather than officially laid down rules and regulations.
Independent channels of communication without specified direction of flow of information are developed by group members.
It emerges spontaneously and is not deliberately created by the management.
It has no definite strucure or form because it is a complex network of social relationships among members.
cards.quote: (a) An informal organisation originates from within the formal organisation as a result of personal interaction among employees. (b) The standards of behaviour evolve from group norms rather than officially laid down rules and regulations. (c) Independent channels of communication without specified direction of flow of information are developed by group members. (d) It emerges spontaneously and is not deliberately created by the management. (e) It has no definite strucure or form because it is a complex network of social relationships among members.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the advantages of the informal organisation.
cards.back:
speed
fulfillment of social needs
fills inadequacies of formal structure
cards.quote: Its advantages are speed, fulfillment of social needs, fills inadequacies of formal structure.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the disadvantages of the informal organisation.
cards.back:
disruptive force
resistance to change
priority to group interests
cards.quote: Its disadvantages are: disruptive force, resistance to change and priority to group interests.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Formal vs informal organisation: the difference on meaning (formal first, informal second).
cards.back:
Structure of authority relationships created by the management
Network of social relationships arising out of interaction among employees
cards.quote: Structure of authority relationships created by the management Network of social relationships arising out of interaction among employees

source.section: Formal and informal organisation: A Comparative view

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Formal vs informal organisation: the difference on behaviour (formal first, informal second).
cards.back:
It is directed by rules
There is no set behaviour pattern
cards.quote: It is directed by rules There is no set behaviour pattern

source.section: Formal and informal organisation: A Comparative view

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Formal vs informal organisation: the difference on nature (formal first, informal second).
cards.back:
Rigid
Flexible
cards.quote: Rigid Flexible

source.section: Formal and informal organisation: A Comparative view

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Formal vs informal organisation: the difference on leadership (formal first, informal second).
cards.back:
Managers are leaders.
Leaders may or may not be managers. They are chosen by the group.
cards.quote: Managers are leaders. Leaders may or may not be managers. They are chosen by the group.

source.section: Formal and informal organisation: A Comparative view

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is delegation?
cards.back: Delegation refers to the downward transfer of authority from a superior to a subordinate.
cards.quote: Delegation refers to the downward transfer of authority from a superior to a subordinate.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define delegation (Louis Allen).
cards.back: Delegation is the process a manager follows in dividing the work assigned to him so that he performs that part which only he because of his unique organisational placement, can perform effectively and so that he can get others to help with what remains.
cards.quote: Delegation is the process a manager follows in dividing the work assigned to him so that he performs that part which only he because of his unique organisational placement, can perform effectively and so that he can get others to help with what remains.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define delegation of authority (Theo Haimman).
cards.back: Delegation of authority merely means the granting of authority to subordinates to operate within prescribed limits.
cards.quote: Delegation of authority merely means the granting of authority to subordinates to operate within prescribed limits.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Delegation does not mean abdication: who remains accountable for the performance of the assigned tasks?
cards.back: However, delegation does not mean abdication. The manager shall still be accountable for the performance of the assigned tasks.
cards.quote: However, delegation does not mean abdication. The manager shall still be accountable for the performance of the assigned tasks.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the elements of delegation.
cards.back:
Authority
Responsibility
Accountability
cards.quote: It has three elements: Authority, Responsibility and Accountability.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is authority (an element of delegation)?
cards.back: Authority refers to the right of an individual to command his subordinates and to take action within the scope of his position.
cards.quote: Authority refers to the right of an individual to command his subordinates and to take action within the scope of his position.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is responsibility (an element of delegation)?
cards.back: Responsibility is the obligation of a subordinate to properly perform the assigned duty.
cards.quote: Responsibility is the obligation of a subordinate to properly perform the assigned duty.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In which direction does responsibility flow, since a subordinate is responsible to his superior?
cards.back:
Upwards
Thus, responsibility flows upwards, i.e., a subordinate will always be responsible to his superior.
cards.quote: Thus, responsibility flows upwards, i.e., a subordinate will always be responsible to his superior.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: For effective delegation, the authority granted must be commensurate with what?
cards.back: Thus, for effective delegation the authority granted must be commensurate with the assigned responsibility.
cards.quote: Thus, for effective delegation the authority granted must be commensurate with the assigned responsibility.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: If authority granted is more than responsibility, it may lead to ____
cards.back: If authority granted is more than responsibility, it may lead to misuse of authority
cards.quote: If authority granted is more than responsibility, it may lead to misuse of authority

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is accountability (an element of delegation)?
cards.back: Accountability implies being answerable for the final outcome.
cards.quote: Accountability implies being answerable for the final outcome.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Accountability: can it be delegated, and in which direction does it flow?
cards.back:
Cannot be delegated; flows upwards
It cannot be delegated and flows upwards, i.e., a subordinate will be accountable to a superior for satisfactory performance of work.
cards.quote: It cannot be delegated and flows upwards, i.e., a subordinate will be accountable to a superior for satisfactory performance of work.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In conclusion, it can be stated that while authority is ____, responsibility is ____, accountability is ____.
cards.back: In conclusion, it can be stated that while authority is delegated, responsibility is assumed, accountability is imposed.
cards.quote: In conclusion, it can be stated that while authority is delegated, responsibility is assumed, accountability is imposed.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Responsibility is derived from ____ and ____ is derived from responsibility.
cards.back: Responsibility is derived from authority and accountability is derived from responsibility.
cards.quote: Responsibility is derived from authority and accountability is derived from responsibility.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five points on the importance of delegation (NCERT chapter summary).
cards.back:
effective management
employee development
motivation
growth
coordination
cards.quote: Importance of delegation is that it helps in effective management, employee development, motivation, growth and coordination.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is decentralisation?
cards.back: Put simply, decentralisation refers to delegation of authority throughout all the levels of the organisation.
cards.quote: Put simply, decentralisation refers to delegation of authority throughout all the levels of the organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define decentralisation (Louis Allen).
cards.back: Decentralisation refers to systematic effort to delegate to the lowest level all authority except that which can be exercised at central points.
cards.quote: Decentralisation refers to systematic effort to delegate to the lowest level all authority except that which can be exercised at central points.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define decentralisation and centralisation (Henri Fayol).
cards.back: Everything which goes to increase the importance of a subordinate's role is decentralisation, everything that goes to reduce it is centralisation.
cards.quote: Everything which goes to increase the importance of a subordinate's role is decentralisation, everything that goes to reduce it is centralisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are organisations called in which decision making authority lies with the top management?
cards.back:
Centralised organisations
Those organisations in which decision making authority lies with the top management are termed as centralised organisations
cards.quote: Those organisations in which decision making authority lies with the top management are termed as centralised organisations

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Can an organisation be completely centralised or completely decentralised, according to NCERT?
cards.back:
Never
An organisation can never be completely centralised or decentralised.
cards.quote: An organisation can never be completely centralised or decentralised.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the points on the importance of decentralisation (NCERT chapter summary).
cards.back:
development of managerial talent
quick decision making
reducing burden on top management
development of initiative
growth
better control
cards.quote: Importance of decentralisation is that it helps in development of managerial talent, quick decision making reducing burden on top management, development of initiative, growth and better control.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Step 4 of organising: once work is allocated, what should each individual also know?
cards.back:
Establishing authority and reporting relationships
Merely allocating work is not enough. Each individual should also know who he has to take orders from and to whom he is accountable.
cards.quote: Merely allocating work is not enough. Each individual should also know who he has to take orders from and to whom he is accountable.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define planning.
cards.back: Planning is deciding in advance what to do and how to do. It is one of the basic managerial functions.
cards.quote: Planning is deciding in advance what to do and how to do. It is one of the basic managerial functions.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning seeks to bridge the ____ between where we are and where we want to go.
cards.back: Planning seeks to bridge the gap between where we are and where we want to go.
cards.quote: Planning seeks to bridge the gap between where we are and where we want to go.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning is what managers at all levels do. It requires taking ____ since it involves making a choice from alternative courses of action.
cards.back: Planning is what managers at all levels do. It requires taking decisions since it involves making a choice from alternative courses of action.
cards.quote: Planning is what managers at all levels do. It requires taking decisions since it involves making a choice from alternative courses of action.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does planning involve?
cards.back: Planning, thus, involves setting objectives and developing appropriate courses of action to achieve these objectives.
cards.quote: Planning, thus, involves setting objectives and developing appropriate courses of action to achieve these objectives.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Give NCERT's comprehensive definition of planning (objectives, courses of action, selection).
cards.back: setting objectives for a given time period, formulating various courses of action to achieve them, and then selecting the best possible alternative from among the various courses of action available.
cards.quote: One of the ways to do so would be to define planning as setting objectives for a given time period, formulating various courses of action to achieve them, and then selecting the best possible alternative from among the various courses of action available.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the six points of importance of planning.
cards.back:
Planning provides directions
reduces risks of uncertainty
reduces overlapping and wasteful activities
promotes innovative ideas
facilitates decision making
establishes standards for controlling
cards.quote: Planning provides directions, reduces risks of uncertainty, reduces overlapping and wasteful activities, promotes innovative ideas, facilitates decision making, establishes standards for controlling.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: By stating in advance how work is to be done planning provides ____ for action.
cards.back: By stating in advance how work is to be done planning provides direction for action.
cards.quote: By stating in advance how work is to be done planning provides direction for action.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning serves as the basis of ____ the activities and efforts of different divisions, departments and individuals.
cards.back: Planning serves as the basis of coordinating the activities and efforts of different divisions, departments and individuals.
cards.quote: Planning serves as the basis of coordinating the activities and efforts of different divisions, departments and individuals.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning helps the manager to look into the future and make a ____ from amongst various alternative courses of action.
cards.back: Planning helps the manager to look into the future and make a choice from amongst various alternative courses of action.
cards.quote: Planning helps the manager to look into the future and make a choice from amongst various alternative courses of action.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning provides the goals or ____ against which actual performance is measured.
cards.back: Planning provides the goals or standards against which actual performance is measured.
cards.quote: Planning provides the goals or standards against which actual performance is measured.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Which function of management does NCERT say planning is a prerequisite for?
cards.back: Therefore, we can say that planning is a prerequisite for controlling.
cards.quote: Therefore, we can say that planning is a prerequisite for controlling.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the seven features of planning (NCERT chapter summary).
cards.back:
Planning focuses on achieving objectives
It is a primary function of management
Planning is pervasive
continuous
futuristic
involves decision making
It is a mental exercise
cards.quote: Planning focuses on achieving objectives; It is a primary function of management; Planning is pervasive, continuous, futuristic and involves decision making; It is a mental exercise.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning precedes other functions. What is this also referred to as?
cards.back:
The primacy of planning
Thus, planning precedes other functions. This is also referred to as the primacy of planning.
cards.quote: Thus, planning precedes other functions. This is also referred to as the primacy of planning.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning is required at ____ of management as well as in all departments of the organisation.
cards.back: Planning is required at all levels of management as well as in all departments of the organisation.
cards.quote: Planning is required at all levels of management as well as in all departments of the organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning is, therefore, regarded as a forward looking function based on ____.
cards.back: Planning is, therefore, regarded as a forward looking function based on forecasting.
cards.quote: Planning is, therefore, regarded as a forward looking function based on forecasting.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning requires application of the mind involving ____, intelligent imagination and sound judgement.
cards.back: Planning requires application of the mind involving foresight, intelligent imagination and sound judgement.
cards.quote: Planning requires application of the mind involving foresight, intelligent imagination and sound judgement.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the six limitations of planning.
cards.back:
Planning leads to rigidity
reduces creativity
involves huge costs
It is a time consuming process
Planning does not work in a dynamic environment
and does not guarantee success
cards.quote: Planning leads to rigidity; reduces creativity; involves huge costs; It is a time consuming process; Planning does not work in a dynamic environment; and does not guarantee success.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The business environment is ____, nothing is constant.
cards.back: The business environment is dynamic, nothing is constant.
cards.quote: The business environment is dynamic, nothing is constant.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Which quality does planning in a way reduce, since people tend to think along the same lines as others?
cards.back:
Creativity
Thus, planning in a way reduces creativity since people tend to think along the same lines as others.
cards.quote: Thus, planning in a way reduces creativity since people tend to think along the same lines as others.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the seven steps in the planning process, in order.
cards.back:
Setting objectives
Developing premises
Identifying alternative courses of action
Evaluating alternative courses
Selecting an alternative
Implement the plan
Follow-up action
cards.quote: Setting objectives: Objectives may be set for the entire organisation and each department or unit within the organisation. Developing premises: Planning is concerned with the future which is uncertain and every planner is using conjucture about what might happen in future. Identifying alternative courses of action: Once objectives are set, assumptions are made. Then the next step would be to act upon them. Evaluating alternative courses: The next step is to weigh the pros and cons of each alternative. Selecting an alternative: This is the real point of decision making. The best plan has to be adopted and implemented. Implement the plan: This is concerned with putting the plan into action. Follow-up action: Monitoring the plans are equally important to ensure that objectives are achieved.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The first and foremost step is setting ____.
cards.back: The first and foremost step is setting objectives.
cards.quote: The first and foremost step is setting objectives.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are the assumptions a manager must make about the future called?
cards.back:
Premises
Therefore, the manager is required to make certain assumptions about the future. These assumptions are called premises.
cards.quote: Therefore, the manager is required to make certain assumptions about the future. These assumptions are called premises.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are premises (assumptions) in planning?
cards.back: Assumptions are the base material upon which plans are to be drawn.
cards.quote: Assumptions are the base material upon which plans are to be drawn.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Planning process: which step involves weighing the pros and cons of each alternative?
cards.back: Evaluating alternative courses: The next step is to weigh the pros and cons of each alternative.
cards.quote: Evaluating alternative courses: The next step is to weigh the pros and cons of each alternative.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In the planning process, which step is the real point of decision making?
cards.back:
Selecting an alternative
Selecting an alternative: This is the real point of decision making. The best plan has to be adopted and implemented.
cards.quote: Selecting an alternative: This is the real point of decision making. The best plan has to be adopted and implemented.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Types of plans, based on what the plans seek to achieve.
cards.back:
Objectives
Strategy
Policy
Procedure
Method
Rule
Programme
Budget
cards.quote: Based on what the plans seek to achieve, plans can be classified as Objectives, Strategy, Policy, Procedure, Method, Rule, Programme, Budget.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Short-term operational plans fall into which two classes?
cards.back:
single-use plans
standing plans
cards.quote: These plans can be classified into single-use plans and standing plans.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a single-use plan?
cards.back: A single-use plan is developed for a one-time event or project.
cards.quote: A single-use plan is developed for a one-time event or project.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Single-use plans include which plans?
cards.back:
budgets
programmes
projects
cards.quote: These plans include budgets, programmes and projects.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a standing plan?
cards.back: A standing plan is used for activities that occur regularly over a period of time. It is designed to ensure that internal operations of an organisation run smoothly.
cards.quote: A standing plan is used for activities that occur regularly over a period of time. It is designed to ensure that internal operations of an organisation run smoothly.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Standing plans include which plans?
cards.back:
policies
procedures
methods
rules
cards.quote: Standing plans include policies, procedures, methods and rules.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are objectives (as a type of plan)?
cards.back: The first step in planning is setting objectives. Objectives, therefore, can be said to be the desired future position that the management would like to reach.
cards.quote: The first step in planning is setting objectives. Objectives, therefore, can be said to be the desired future position that the management would like to reach.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Objectives are defined as what?
cards.back: Objectives are very basic to the organisation and they are defined as ends which the management seeks to achieve by its operations.
cards.quote: Objectives are very basic to the organisation and they are defined as ends which the management seeks to achieve by its operations.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Objectives need to be expressed in specific terms i.e., they should be measurable in ____ terms
cards.back: Objectives need to be expressed in specific terms i.e., they should be measurable in quantitative terms
cards.quote: Objectives need to be expressed in specific terms i.e., they should be measurable in quantitative terms

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a strategy (as a type of plan)?
cards.back: A strategy provides the broad contours of an organisation's business. It will also refer to future decisions defining the organisations direction and scope in the long run.
cards.quote: A strategy provides the broad contours of an organisation's business. It will also refer to future decisions defining the organisations direction and scope in the long run.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the three dimensions of a strategy.
cards.back:
determining long term objectives
adopting a particular course of action
allocating resources necessary to achieve the objective
cards.quote: This comprehensive plan will include three dimensions, (i) determining long term objectives, (ii) adopting a particular course of action, and (iii) allocating resources necessary to achieve the objective.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What major strategic decisions does an organisation take?
cards.back:
whether the organisation will continue to be in the same line of business
combine new lines of activity with the existing business
seek to acquire a dominant position in the same market
cards.quote: Major strategic decisions will include decisions like whether the organisation will continue to be in the same line of business, or combine new lines of activity with the existing business or seek to acquire a dominant position in the same market.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are policies (as a type of plan)?
cards.back: Policies are general statements that guide thinking or channelise energies towards a particular direction.
cards.quote: Policies are general statements that guide thinking or channelise energies towards a particular direction.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Example: a recruitment policy and a pricing policy. Name the concept.
cards.back: the company may have a recruitment policy, pricing policy within which objectives are set and decisions are made.
cards.quote: For example, the company may have a recruitment policy, pricing policy within which objectives are set and decisions are made.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Major vs minor company policies: who are they meant for?
cards.back: Major company policies are for all to know i.e., customers, clients, competitors etc., whereas minor polices are applicable to insiders and contain minute details of information vital to the employees of an organisation.
cards.quote: Major company policies are for all to know i.e., customers, clients, competitors etc., whereas minor polices are applicable to insiders and contain minute details of information vital to the employees of an organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are procedures (as a type of plan)?
cards.back: Procedures are routine steps on how to carry out activities. They detail the exact manner in which any work is to be performed. They are specified in a chronological order.
cards.quote: Procedures are routine steps on how to carry out activities. They detail the exact manner in which any work is to be performed. They are specified in a chronological order.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Example: requisitioning supplies before production is which type of plan?
cards.back: there may be a procedure for requisitioning supplies before production.
cards.quote: For example, there may be a procedure for requisitioning supplies before production.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are methods (as a type of plan)?
cards.back: Methods provide the prescribed ways or manner in which a task has to be performed considering the objective.
cards.quote: Methods provide the prescribed ways or manner in which a task has to be performed considering the objective.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are rules (as a type of plan)?
cards.back: Rules are specific statements that inform what is to be done. They do not allow for any flexibility or discretion.
cards.quote: Rules are specific statements that inform what is to be done. They do not allow for any flexibility or discretion.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: NCERT example: reporting for work at a particular time. Which standing plan is this?
cards.back: Rules are very clearly stated as to exactly what has to be done like reporting for work at a particular time.
cards.quote: Rules are very clearly stated as to exactly what has to be done like reporting for work at a particular time.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are programmes (as a type of plan)?
cards.back: Programmes are detailed statements about a project which outlines the objectives, policies, procedures, rules, tasks, human and physical resources required and the budget to implement any course of action.
cards.quote: Programmes are detailed statements about a project which outlines the objectives, policies, procedures, rules, tasks, human and physical resources required and the budget to implement any course of action.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a budget (as a type of plan)?
cards.back: A budget is a statement of expected results expressed in numerical terms. It is a plan which quantifies future facts and figures.
cards.quote: A budget is a statement of expected results expressed in numerical terms. It is a plan which quantifies future facts and figures.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is the cash budget?
cards.back: The cash budget is a basic tool in the management of cash. It is a device to help the management to plan and control the use of cash.
cards.quote: The cash budget is a basic tool in the management of cash. It is a device to help the management to plan and control the use of cash.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The cash budget is a statement showing what?
cards.back: a statement showing the estimated cash inflows and cash outflows over a given period.
cards.quote: It is a statement showing the estimated cash inflows and cash outflows over a given period.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Formula: net cash position in the cash budget.
cards.back: inflows minus (–) outflows = surplus or deficiency.
cards.quote: The net cash position is determined by the cash budget i.e., inflows minus (–) outflows = surplus or deficiency.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: When a strategy is formulated, what must be taken into consideration, and what will affect an organisation's strategy?
cards.back: Whenever a strategy is formulated, the business environment needs to be taken into consideration. The changes in the economic, political, social, legal and technological environment will affect an organisation's strategy.
cards.quote: Whenever a strategy is formulated, the business environment needs to be taken into consideration. The changes in the economic, political, social, legal and technological environment will affect an organisation's strategy.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define a managerial principle.
cards.back: A managerial principle is a broad and general guideline for decision-making and behaviour.
cards.quote: A managerial principle is a broad and general guideline for decision-making and behaviour.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are techniques of management?
cards.back: Techniques are procedures or methods, which involve a series of steps to be taken to accomplish desired goals.
cards.quote: Techniques are procedures or methods, which involve a series of steps to be taken to accomplish desired goals.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Principles are ____ to take decisions or actions while practicing techniques.
cards.back: Principles are guidelines to take decisions or actions while practicing techniques.
cards.quote: Principles are guidelines to take decisions or actions while practicing techniques.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are values, in contrast to principles?
cards.back: Values are something, which are acceptable or desirable. They have moral connotations.
cards.quote: Values are something, which are acceptable or desirable. They have moral connotations.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Values vs principles of management: how each is formed.
cards.back: Values are general rules for behaviour of individuals in society formed through common practice whereas principles of management are formed after research in work situations, which are technical in nature.
cards.quote: Values are general rules for behaviour of individuals in society formed through common practice whereas principles of management are formed after research in work situations, which are technical in nature.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What are principles of management, by nature?
cards.back: Principles are general propositions, which are applicable when certain conditions are present.
cards.quote: Principles are general propositions, which are applicable when certain conditions are present.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: On what basis have the principles of management been developed?
cards.back:
Observation and experimentation, and managers' personal experiences
These have been developed on the basis of observation and experimentation as well as personal experiences of the managers.
cards.quote: These have been developed on the basis of observation and experimentation as well as personal experiences of the managers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Derivation of these principles may be said to be a matter of ____ and their creative application may be regarded as an ____.
cards.back: Derivation of these principles may be said to be a matter of science and their creative application may be regarded as an art.
cards.quote: Derivation of these principles may be said to be a matter of science and their creative application may be regarded as an art.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What kind of relationship do the principles of management denote?
cards.back:
Cause and effect
These principles are guidelines to action. They denote a cause and effect relationship.
cards.quote: These principles are guidelines to action. They denote a cause and effect relationship.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the 7 points on the nature of principles of management.
cards.back:
formed by practice
general guidelines
universal
flexible
behavioural
contingent
cause and effect relationship
cards.quote: The nature of management principles can be discussed under the heads- formed by practice; general guidelines; universal; flexible; behavioural; contingent; and cause and effect relationship

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The principles of management are intended to apply to ____, business as well as non-business
cards.back: The principles of management are intended to apply to all types of organisations, business as well as non-business
cards.quote: The principles of management are intended to apply to all types of organisations, business as well as non-business

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: As general guidelines, what do principles of management not provide?
cards.back:
Readymade, straitjacket solutions to all managerial problems
The principles are guidelines to action but do not provide readymade, straitjacket solutions to all managerial problems.
cards.quote: The principles are guidelines to action but do not provide readymade, straitjacket solutions to all managerial problems.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The principles of management are formed by ____ and collective wisdom of managers as well as ____.
cards.back: The principles of management are formed by experience and collective wisdom of managers as well as experimentation.
cards.quote: The principles of management are formed by experience and collective wisdom of managers as well as experimentation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Principles of management are not rigid prescriptions. Which nature point is this?
cards.back:
Flexible
The principles of management are not rigid prescriptions, which have to be followed absolutely. They are flexible and can be modified by the manager when the situation so demands.
cards.quote: The principles of management are not rigid prescriptions, which have to be followed absolutely. They are flexible and can be modified by the manager when the situation so demands.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Management principles aim at influencing behaviour of human beings. Therefore, principles of management are mainly ____ in nature.
cards.back: Management principles aim at influencing behaviour of human beings. Therefore, principles of management are mainly behavioural in nature.
cards.quote: Management principles aim at influencing behaviour of human beings. Therefore, principles of management are mainly behavioural in nature.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The principles of management are intended to establish relationship between ____
cards.back: The principles of management are intended to establish relationship between cause and effect
cards.quote: The principles of management are intended to establish relationship between cause and effect

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The application of principles of management is ____ or dependent upon the prevailing situation at a particular point of time.
cards.back: The application of principles of management is contingent or dependent upon the prevailing situation at a particular point of time.
cards.quote: The application of principles of management is contingent or dependent upon the prevailing situation at a particular point of time.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the 8 points on the significance of principles of management.
cards.back:
Increase in efficiency
Optimum utilisation of resources
Scientific decision making
Adaptation to changing environment
Fulfilling social responsibilities
Proper research and development
Training managers
Effective administration
cards.quote: The significance can be discussed under the following heads- Increase in efficiency; Optimum utilisation of resources; Scientific decision making; Adaptation to changing environment; Fulfilling social responsibilities; Proper research and development; Training managers; and Effective administration.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is meant by optimum use of resources?
cards.back: By optimum use we mean that the resources should be put to use in such a manner that they should give maximum benefit with minimum cost.
cards.quote: By optimum use we mean that the resources should be put to use in such a manner that they should give maximum benefit with minimum cost.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The increased awareness of the public, forces businesses especially limited companies to fulfill their ____.
cards.back: The increased awareness of the public, forces businesses especially limited companies to fulfill their social responsibilities.
cards.quote: The increased awareness of the public, forces businesses especially limited companies to fulfill their social responsibilities.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the other two streams of the classical school besides scientific management.
cards.back: The other two streams belonging to the classical school are Fayol's Administrative Theory and Max Weber's Bureaucracy.
cards.quote: The other two streams belonging to the classical school are Fayol's Administrative Theory and Max Weber's Bureaucracy.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What were F.W. Taylor and Henri Fayol by profession?
cards.back: Whereas F.W. Taylor was an American mechanical engineer, Henri Fayol was a French mining engineer.
cards.quote: Whereas F.W. Taylor was an American mechanical engineer, Henri Fayol was a French mining engineer.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Taylor thought that by scientifically analysing work, it would be possible to find `____' to do it.
cards.back: Taylor thought that by scientifically analysing work, it would be possible to find `one best way' to do it.
cards.quote: Taylor thought that by scientifically analysing work, it would be possible to find `one best way' to do it.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is Taylor most remembered for?
cards.back: He is most remembered for his time and motion studies.
cards.quote: He is most remembered for his time and motion studies.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Which term did Taylor coin, in which article and year?
cards.back: He is known for coinage of the term `Scientific Management' in his article `The Principles of Scientific Management' published in 1911.
cards.quote: He is known for coinage of the term `Scientific Management' in his article `The Principles of Scientific Management' published in 1911.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is meant by the `rule of thumb'?
cards.back: In the earlier days of the Industrial Revolution, in the absence of an established theory of factory organisation, factory owners or managers relied on personal judgment in attending to the problems they confronted in the course of managing their work. This is what is referred to as `rule of thumb'.
cards.quote: In the earlier days of the Industrial Revolution, in the absence of an established theory of factory organisation, factory owners or managers relied on personal judgment in attending to the problems they confronted in the course of managing their work. This is what is referred to as `rule of thumb'.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Who is the `Father of Scientific Management'?
cards.back: In this scenario, Taylor emerged as the `Father of Scientific Management'.
cards.quote: In this scenario, Taylor emerged as the `Father of Scientific Management'.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does scientific management imply?
cards.back: It implies conducting business activities according to standardised tools, methods and trained personnel in order to increase the output, improve its quality and reduce costs and wastes.
cards.quote: It implies conducting business activities according to standardised tools, methods and trained personnel in order to increase the output, improve its quality and reduce costs and wastes.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define scientific management (F.W. Taylor).
cards.back: Scientific management means knowing exactly what you want men to do and seeing that they do it in the best and cheapest way.
cards.quote: Scientific management means knowing exactly what you want men to do and seeing that they do it in the best and cheapest way.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: By how much did productivity rise at Bethlehem Steel under scientific management?
cards.back: The Bethlehem Steel company where Taylor himself worked achieved three-fold increase in productivity by application of scientific management principles.
cards.quote: The Bethlehem Steel company where Taylor himself worked achieved three-fold increase in productivity by application of scientific management principles.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name Taylor's 5 principles of scientific management.
cards.back:
Science, not the rule of thumb
Harmony not discord
Cooperation not individualism
Maximum not restricted output
Development of each person to her/ his greatest efficiency and prosperity
cards.quote: Taylor's principles of scientific management are -- Science, not the rule of thumb; Harmony not discord; Cooperation not individualism; Maximum not restricted output; Development of each person to her/ his greatest efficiency and prosperity.
cards.note: The chapter text headings give four principles; the summary list adds 'Maximum not restricted output'.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In 'Science not Rule of Thumb', traditional methods were investigated through what?
cards.back:
Work-study
Scientific method involved investigation of traditional methods through work-study, unifying the best practices and developing a standard method
cards.quote: Scientific method involved investigation of traditional methods through work-study, unifying the best practices and developing a standard method

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: To achieve this state, Taylor called for complete ____ on the part of both management and workers.
cards.back: To achieve this state, Taylor called for complete mental revolution on the part of both management and workers.
cards.quote: To achieve this state, Taylor called for complete mental revolution on the part of both management and workers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Which Taylor principle is `Cooperation, Not Individualism' an extension of?
