cards.back: There should be complete cooperation between the labour and the management instead of individualism. This principle is an extension of principle of `Harmony not discord'.
cards.quote: There should be complete cooperation between the labour and the management instead of individualism. This principle is an extension of principle of `Harmony not discord'.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the 7 techniques of scientific management (Taylor).
cards.back:
Functional foremanship
Standardisation and simplification of work
Fatigue Study
Method Study
Time Study
Motion Study
Differential Wage System
cards.quote: The techniques of scientific management as per Taylor were -- Functional foremanship; Standardisation and simplification of work; Fatigue Study; Method Study; Time Study; Motion Study; and Differential Wage System.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is functional foremanship?
cards.back: Taylor advocated separation of planning and execution functions. This concept was extended to the lowest level of the shop floor. It was known as functional foremanship.
cards.quote: Taylor advocated separation of planning and execution functions. This concept was extended to the lowest level of the shop floor. It was known as functional foremanship.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four specialists under the planning in-charge and their roles.
cards.back: Under planning incharge four personnel namely instruction card clerk, route clerk, time and cost clerk and a disciplinarian worked. These four personnel would draft instructions for the workers, specify the route of production, prepare time and cost sheet and ensure discipline respectively.
cards.quote: Under planning incharge four personnel namely instruction card clerk, route clerk, time and cost clerk and a disciplinarian worked. These four personnel would draft instructions for the workers, specify the route of production, prepare time and cost sheet and ensure discipline respectively.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four specialists under the production in-charge and their roles.
cards.back: Under Production incharge, personnel who would work were speed boss, gang boss, repair boss, and inspector. These respectively were responsible for timely and accurate completion of job, keeping machines and tools etc., ready for operation by workers, ensure proper working condition of machines and tools and check the quality of work.
cards.quote: Under Production incharge, personnel who would work were speed boss, gang boss, repair boss, and inspector. These respectively were responsible for timely and accurate completion of job, keeping machines and tools etc., ready for operation by workers, ensure proper working condition of machines and tools and check the quality of work.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Functional foremanship is an extension of the principle of ____ to the shop floor.
cards.back: Functional foremanship is an extension of the principle of division of work and specialisation to the shop floor.
cards.quote: Functional foremanship is an extension of the principle of division of work and specialisation to the shop floor.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Functional foremanship: how many specialists did Taylor propose?
cards.back: Since all these qualities could not be found in a single person so Taylor proposed eight specialists.
cards.quote: Since all these qualities could not be found in a single person so Taylor proposed eight specialists.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define standardisation as a technique of scientific management.
cards.back: Standardisation refers to the process of setting standards for every business activity; it can be standardisation of process, raw material, time, product, machinery, methods or working conditions.
cards.quote: Standardisation refers to the process of setting standards for every business activity; it can be standardisation of process, raw material, time, product, machinery, methods or working conditions.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four objectives of standardisation.
cards.back:
(i) To reduce a given line or product to fixed types, sizes and characteristics.
(ii) To establish interchangeability of manufactured parts and products.
(iii) To establish standards of excellence and quality in materials.
(iv) To establish standards of performance of men and machines.
cards.quote: (i) To reduce a given line or product to fixed types, sizes and characteristics. (ii) To establish interchangeability of manufactured parts and products. (iii) To establish standards of excellence and quality in materials. (iv) To establish standards of performance of men and machines.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Simplification vs standardisation: the difference in aim.
cards.back: Simplification aims at eliminating superfluous varieties, sizes and dimensions while standardisation implies devising new varieties instead of the existing ones.
cards.quote: Simplification aims at eliminating superfluous varieties, sizes and dimensions while standardisation implies devising new varieties instead of the existing ones.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The objective of method study is to find out ____ of doing the job.
cards.back: The objective of method study is to find out one best way of doing the job.
cards.quote: The objective of method study is to find out one best way of doing the job.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Taylor devised the concept of ____ by using method study.
cards.back: Taylor devised the concept of assembly line by using method study.
cards.quote: Taylor devised the concept of assembly line by using method study.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define motion study.
cards.back: Motion study refers to the study of movements like lifting, putting objects, sitting and changing positions, etc., which are undertaken while doing a typical job.
cards.quote: Motion study refers to the study of movements like lifting, putting objects, sitting and changing positions, etc., which are undertaken while doing a typical job.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Taylor and Gailberth reduced motions in brick layering from 18 to how many?
cards.back:
5
Taylor and his associate Frank Gailberth were able to reduce motions in brick layering from 18 to just 5.
cards.quote: Taylor and his associate Frank Gailberth were able to reduce motions in brick layering from 18 to just 5.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Types of body motions found in a motion study.
cards.back:
(i) Motions which are productive
(ii) Motions which are incidental (e.g., going to stores)
(iii) Motions which are unproductive
cards.quote: (i) Motions which are productive (ii) Motions which are incidental (e.g., going to stores) (iii) Motions which are unproductive.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define time study.
cards.back: It determines the standard time taken to perform a well-defined job.
cards.quote: It determines the standard time taken to perform a well-defined job.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the objectives of time study.
cards.back:
to determine the number of workers to be employed
frame suitable incentive schemes
determine labour costs
cards.quote: The objective of time study is to determine the number of workers to be employed; frame suitable incentive schemes and determine labour costs.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define fatigue study.
cards.back: Fatigue study seeks to determine the amount and frequency of rest intervals in completing a task.
cards.quote: Fatigue study seeks to determine the amount and frequency of rest intervals in completing a task.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Which wage system did Taylor advocate to differentiate efficient from inefficient workers?
cards.back:
Differential piece wage system
Taylor was a strong advocate of piece wage system. He wanted to differentiate between efficient and inefficient workers.
cards.quote: Taylor was a strong advocate of piece wage system. He wanted to differentiate between efficient and inefficient workers.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define mental revolution (Taylor).
cards.back: Mental revolution involves a change in the attitude of workers and management towards one another from competition to cooperation.
cards.quote: Mental revolution involves a change in the attitude of workers and management towards one another from competition to cooperation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Who was Henri Fayol?
cards.back: Henri Fayol (1841-1925) was a French management theorist whose theories concerning scientific organisation of labour were widely influential in the beginning of twentieth century.
cards.quote: Henri Fayol (1841-1925) was a French management theorist whose theories concerning scientific organisation of labour were widely influential in the beginning of twentieth century.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the functions of management according to Fayol.
cards.back:
to plan
to organise
to command
to coordinate
to control
cards.quote: According to Fayol, the functions of management are to plan, to organise, to command, to coordinate and to control.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Into which activities could Fayol divide all activities of an industrial undertaking?
cards.back:
Technical
Commercial
Financial
Security
Accounting
Managerial
cards.quote: According to Fayol, all activities of an industrial undertaking could be divided into: Technical; Commercial; Financial; Security; Accounting and Managerial.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the qualities a manager must possess, as suggested by Fayol.
cards.back:
Physical
Moral
Education
Knowledge and experience
cards.quote: He also suggested that qualities a manager must possess should be -- Physical, Moral, Education, Knowledge and experience.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: How many management principles did Fayol believe could help improve an organisation's operation?
cards.back: He believed that the number of management principles that might help to improve an organisation's operation is potentially limitless.
cards.quote: He believed that the number of management principles that might help to improve an organisation's operation is potentially limitless.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Who is known as the `Father of General Management'?
cards.back: For his contribution he is also known as the `Father of General Management'
cards.quote: For his contribution he is also known as the `Father of General Management'

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name Fayol's 14 principles of management.
cards.back:
Division of work
Authority and responsibility
Discipline
Unity of command
Unity of direction
Subordination of individual interest to general interest
Remuneration of Personnel
Centralisation and decentralisation
Scalar Chain
Order
Equity
Stability in the tenure of Personnel
Initiative
Espirit De corps
cards.quote: Fayol listed 14 principles of management -- Division of work; Authority and responsibility; Discipline; Unity of command; Unity of direction; Subordination of individual interest to general interest; Remuneration of Personnel; Centralisation and decentralisation; Scalar Chain; Order; Equity; Stability in the tenure of Personnel; Initiative; and Espirit De corps.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Work is divided into small tasks/ jobs. A trained specialist who is competent is required to perform each job. Thus, division of work leads to ____.
cards.back: Work is divided into small tasks/ jobs. A trained specialist who is competent is required to perform each job. Thus, division of work leads to specialisation.
cards.quote: Work is divided into small tasks/ jobs. A trained specialist who is competent is required to perform each job. Thus, division of work leads to specialisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: The intent of division of work is to produce more and better work for the same effort. ____ is the most efficient way to use human effort.
cards.back: The intent of division of work is to produce more and better work for the same effort. Specialisation is the most efficient way to use human effort.
cards.quote: The intent of division of work is to produce more and better work for the same effort. Specialisation is the most efficient way to use human effort.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define authority and responsibility (Fayol).
cards.back: Authority is the right to give orders and obtain obedience, and responsibility is the corollary of authority.
cards.quote: Authority is the right to give orders and obtain obedience, and responsibility is the corollary of authority.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Types of authority (Fayol).
cards.back:
official authority, which is the authority to command
personal authority which is the authority of the individual manager
cards.quote: The two types of authority are official authority, which is the authority to command, and personal authority which is the authority of the individual manager.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Managers require authority commensurate with their responsibility. There should be a ____ between authority and responsibility.
cards.back: Managers require authority commensurate with their responsibility. There should be a balance between authority and responsibility.
cards.quote: Managers require authority commensurate with their responsibility. There should be a balance between authority and responsibility.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define discipline (Fayol).
cards.back: Discipline is the obedience to organisational rules and employment agreement which are necessary for the working of the organisation.

good superiors at all levels
clear and fair agreements
judicious application of penalties

cards.front: Define the principle of unity of command.

cards.quote: The principle of unity of command states that each participant in a formal organisation should receive orders from and be responsible to only one superior.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define the principle of unity of direction.
cards.back: All the units of an organisation should be moving towards the same objectives through coordinated and focussed efforts. Each group of activities having the same objective must have one head and one plan.
cards.quote: All the units of an organisation should be moving towards the same objectives through coordinated and focussed efforts. Each group of activities having the same objective must have one head and one plan.

One subordinate should receive orders from and should be responsible to only one superior.

It prevents dual subordination.
It prevents overlapping of activities.

cards.front: Define centralisation and decentralisation.
cards.back: The concentration of decision-making authority is called centralisation whereas its dispersal among more than one person is known as decentralisation.
cards.quote: The concentration of decision-making authority is called centralisation whereas its dispersal among more than one person is known as decentralisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In general large organisations have more ____ than small organisations.
cards.back: In general large organisations have more decentralisation than small organisations.

cards.quote: The principle of order states that `A place for everything (everyone) and everything (everyone) in its (her/his) place'.

cards.back: Employee turnover should be minimised to maintain organisational efficiency
cards.quote: Employee turnover should be minimised to maintain organisational efficiency

cards.back: Initiative means taking the first step with self-motivation. It is thinking out and executing the plan.
cards.quote: Initiative means taking the first step with self-motivation. It is thinking out and executing the plan.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: A good company should have an ____ whereby initiative/suggestions which result in substantial cost/time reduction should be rewarded.
cards.back: A good company should have an employee suggestion system whereby initiative/suggestions which result in substantial cost/time reduction should be rewarded.
cards.quote: A good company should have an employee suggestion system whereby initiative/suggestions which result in substantial cost/time reduction should be rewarded.

cards.front: Management should promote a team spirit of ____ among employees, according to Fayol.
cards.back: Management should promote a team spirit of unity and harmony among employees, according to Fayol.
cards.quote: Management should promote a team spirit of unity and harmony among employees, according to Fayol.

cards.subject: business_studies

cards.back: A manager should replace `I' with `We' in all his conversations with workers to foster team spirit.
cards.quote: A manager should replace `I' with `We' in all his conversations with workers to foster team spirit.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is the principle of equity (Fayol)?

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is staffing, in the simplest terms?
cards.back: In the simplest terms, staffing is 'putting people to jobs'.
cards.quote: In the simplest terms, staffing is 'putting people to jobs'.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: How has staffing been described as a managerial function?
cards.back: Staffing has been described as the managerial function of filling and keeping filled the positions in the organisation structure.
cards.quote: Staffing has been described as the managerial function of filling and keeping filled the positions in the organisation structure.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Staffing is that part of the process of management which is concerned with ____, ____ and ____ a satisfactory and satisfied work force.
cards.back: Staffing is that part of the process of management which is concerned with obtaining, utilising and maintaining a satisfactory and satisfied work force.
cards.quote: Staffing is that part of the process of management which is concerned with obtaining, utilising and maintaining a satisfactory and satisfied work force.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Staffing begins with workforce planning. Name the functions it includes.
cards.back:
recruitment
selection
training
development
promotion
compensation
performance appraisal of work force
cards.quote: It begins with workforce planning and includes different other function like recruitment, selection, training, development, promotion, compensation and performance appraisal of work force.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In a new enterprise, staffing follows which two functions?
cards.back: In a new enterprise, the staffing function follows the planning and organising functions.
cards.quote: In a new enterprise, the staffing function follows the planning and organising functions.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: In an existing enterprise, staffing is a ____ process because new jobs may be created and some of the existing employees may leave the organisation.
cards.back: In an existing enterprise, staffing is a continuous process because new jobs may be created and some of the existing employees may leave the organisation.
cards.quote: In an existing enterprise, staffing is a continuous process because new jobs may be created and some of the existing employees may leave the organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five benefits proper staffing ensures to the organisation.
cards.quote: Proper staffing ensures the following benefits to the organisation: (i) helps in discovering and obtaining competent personnel for various jobs; (ii) makes for higher performance, by putting right person on the right job; (iii) ensures the continuous survival and growth of the enterprise through the succession planning for managers; (iv) helps to ensure optimum utilisation of the human resources. By avoiding overmanning, it prevents under-utilisation of personnel and high labour costs. At the same time it avoids disruption of work by indicating in advance the shortages of personnel; and (v) improves job satisfaction and morale of employees through objective assessment and fair reward for their contribution.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Human resources are the most important ____ of an organisation.
cards.back: Human resources are the most important asset of an organisation.
cards.quote: Human resources are the most important asset of an organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Why has the staffing function assumed greater importance these days?
cards.back: The staffing function has assumed greater importance these days because of rapid advancement of technology, increasing size of organisation and complicated behaviour of human beings.
cards.quote: The staffing function has assumed greater importance these days because of rapid advancement of technology, increasing size of organisation and complicated behaviour of human beings.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: No organisation can be successful unless it can fill and ____ the various positions provided for in the structure with the ____ of people.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Steps in the staffing process (chapter summary): the first five, in order.
cards.back:
Estimating the Manpower Requirements
Recruitment
Selection
Placement and Orientation
Training and Development
cards.quote: Staffing Process: The prime concern of the staffing function in the management process is the timely fulfillment of the manpower requirements within an organisation. Estimating the Manpower Requirements: Performance of each job necessitates the appointment of a person with a specific set of educational qualifications, skills, prior experience and so on. Operationally, understanding the manpower requirements would necessitate workload analysis on the one hand and workforce analysis on the other. Recruitment: Recruitment may be defined as the process of searching for prospective employees and stimulating them to apply for jobs in the organisation. Selection: Selection is the process of choosing from among the pool of the prospective job candidates developed at the stage of recruitment. Placement and Orientation: Orientation is introducing the selected employee to other employees and familiarising him with the rules and policies of the organisation. Placement refers to the employee occupying the position or post for which the person has been selected. Training and Development: What people seek is not simply a job but a career. Every one must have the opportunity to rise to the top. The best way to provide such an opportunity is to facilitate employee learning.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Steps in the staffing process after training and development, in order.
cards.back:
Performance Appraisal
Promotion and career planning
Compensation
cards.quote: (vi) Performance Appraisal After the employees have undergone a period of training and they have been on the job for some time, there is a need to evaluate their performance. All organisations have some formal or informal means of appraising their employee’s performance. Performance appraisal means evaluating an employee’s current and/or past performance as against certain predetermined standards. The employee is expected to know what the standards are and the superior is to provide the employee feedback on his/her performance. The performance appraisal process, therefore, will include defining the job, appraising performance and providing feedback. (vii) Promotion and career planning It becomes necessary for all organisations to address career related issues and promotional avenues for their employees. Managers need to design activities to serve employees’ long-term interests also. They must encourage employees to grow and realise their full potential. Promotions are an integral part of people’s career. They refer to being placed in positions of increased responsibility. They usually mean more pay, responsibility and job satisfaction. (viii) Compensation All organisations need to establish wage and salary plans for their employees.

transfers
promotions

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is a transfer, as an internal source of recruitment?
cards.back: It involves shifting of an employee from one job to another, one department to another or from one shift to another, without a substantive change in the responsibilities and status of the employee.
cards.quote: It involves shifting of an employee from one job to another, one department to another or from one shift to another, without a substantive change in the responsibilities and status of the employee.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does promotion lead to (as an internal source of recruitment)?
cards.back: Promotion leads to shifting an employee to a higher position, carrying higher responsibilities, facilities, status and pay.
cards.quote: Promotion leads to shifting an employee to a higher position, carrying higher responsibilities, facilities, status and pay.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Promotion is a ____ shifting of employees.
cards.back: Promotion is a vertical shifting of employees.
cards.quote: Promotion is a vertical shifting of employees.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five merits of internal sources of recruitment.
cards.back:
Employees are motivated to improve their performance.
Internal recruitment also simplifies the process of selection and placement.
Transfer is a tool of training the employees to prepare them for higher jobs.
Transfer has the benefit of shifting workforce from the surplus departments to those where there is shortage of staff;
Filling of jobs internally is cheaper as compared to getting candidates from external sources.
cards.quote: Filling vacancies in higher jobs from within the organisation or through internal transfers has the following merits: (i) Employees are motivated to improve their performance. A promotion at a higher level may lead to a chain of promotion at lower levels in the organisation. This motivates the employees to improve their performance through learning and practice. Employees work with commitment and loyalty and remain satisfied with their jobs. Also peace prevails in the enterprise because of promotional avenues; (ii) Internal recruitment also simplifies the process of selection and placement. The candidates that are already working in the enterprise can be evaluated more accurately and economically. This is a more reliable way of recruitment since the candidates are already known to the organisation; (iii) Transfer is a tool of training the employees to prepare them for higher jobs. Also people recruited from within the organisation do not need induction training; (iv) Transfer has the benefit of shifting workforce from the surplus departments to those where there is shortage of staff; (v) Filling of jobs internally is cheaper as compared to getting candidates from external sources.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five limitations of internal sources of recruitment.
cards.quote: The limitations of using internal sources of recruitment are as follows: (i) When vacancies are filled through internal promotions, the scope for induction of fresh talent is reduced. Hence, complete reliance on internal recruitment involves danger of ‘inbreeding’ by stopping ‘infusion of new blood’ into the organisation; (ii) The employees may become lethargic if they are sure of time-bound promotions; (iii) A new enterprise cannot use internal sources of recruitment. No organisation can fill all its vacancies from internal sources; (iv) The spirit of competition among the employees may be hampered; and (v) Frequent transfers of employees may often reduce the productivity of the organisation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four merits of external sources of recruitment.
cards.back:
Qualified Personnel
Wider Choice
Fresh Talent
Competitive Spirit
cards.quote: The advantages of using external sources of recruitment are as follows: (i) Qualified Personnel: By using external sources of recruitment, the management can attract qualified and trained people to apply for vacant jobs in the organisation. (ii) Wider Choice: When vacancies are advertised widely, a large number of applicants from outside the organisation apply. The management has a wider choice while selecting the people for employment. (iii) Fresh Talent: The present employees may be insufficient or they may not fulfill the specifications of the jobs to be filled. External recruitment provide wider choice and brings new blood in the organisation. However, it is expensive and time-consuming. (iv) Competitive Spirit: If a company taps external sources, the extisting staff will have to compete with the outsiders. They will work harder to show better performance.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the three limitations of external sources of recruitment.
cards.back:
Dissatisfaction among existing staff
Lengthy process
Costly process
cards.quote: 1. Dissatisfaction among existing staff: External recruitment may lead to dissatisfaction and frustration among existing employees. They may feel that their chances of promotion are reduced. 2. Lengthy process: Recruitment from external sources takes a long time. The business has to notify the vacancies and wait for applications to initiate the selection process. 3. Costly process: It is very costly to recruit staff from external sources. A lot of money has to be spent on advertisement and processing of applications.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define training and development.
cards.back: Training and Development is an attempt to improve the current or future employee performance by increasing an employee's ability to perform through learning, usually by changing the employee's attitude or increasing his or her skills and knowledge.
cards.quote: Training and Development is an attempt to improve the current or future employee performance by increasing an employee's ability to perform through learning, usually by changing the employee's attitude or increasing his or her skills and knowledge.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the five benefits of training and development to the organisation.
cards.back:
Training is a systematic learning, always better than hit and trial methods which lead to wastage of efforts and money.
It enhances employee productivity both in terms of quantity and quality, leading to higher profits.
Training equips the future manager who can take over in case of emergency.
Training increases employee morale and reduces absenteeism and employee turnover.
It helps in obtaining effective response to fast changing environment - technological and economic.
cards.quote: The benefits of training and development to an organisation are as follows: (i) Training is a systematic learning, always better than hit and trial methods which lead to wastage of efforts and money. (ii) It enhances employee productivity both in terms of quantity and quality, leading to higher profits. (iii) Training equips the future manager who can take over in case of emergency. (iv) Training increases employee morale and reduces absenteeism and employee turnover. (v) It helps in obtaining effective response to fast changing environment – technological and economic.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Name the four benefits of training and development to the employee.
cards.back:
Improved skills and knowledge due to training lead to better career of the individual.
Increased performance by the individual help him to earn more.
Training makes the employee more efficient to handle machines. Thus, less prone to accidents.
Training increases the satisfaction and morale of employees.

(ii) Increased performance by the individual help him to earn more. (iii) Training makes the employee more efficient to handle machines. Thus, less prone to accidents. (iv) Training increases the satisfaction and morale of employees.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define training.
cards.back: Training is any process by which the aptitudes, skills and abilities of employees to perform specific jobs are increased.
cards.quote: Training is any process by which the aptitudes, skills and abilities of employees to perform specific jobs are increased.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Define education (in the context of training and development).
cards.back: Education is the process of increasing the knowledge and understanding of employees. It is the understanding and interpretation of knowledge.
cards.quote: Education is the process of increasing the knowledge and understanding of employees. It is the understanding and interpretation of knowledge.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What does development refer to?
cards.back: Development refers to the learning opportunities designed to help employees grow.
cards.quote: Development refers to the learning opportunities designed to help employees grow.

cards.front: Training vs development: what is each a process of? (Training first, then Development.)
cards.back: It is a process of increasing knowledge and skills. It is a process of learning and growth.

cards.front: Training methods are broadly categorised into which two groups?

On-the-Job
Off-the-Job
cards.quote: There are various methods of training. These are broadly categorised into two groups: On-the-Job and Off-the-Job methods.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: On-the-Job vs Off-the-Job training methods: the difference.
cards.back: On-the-Job methods refer to the methods that are applied to the workplace, while the employee is actually working. Off-the-Job methods are used away from the work place. The former means learning while doing, while the latter means learning before doing.
cards.quote: On-the-Job methods refer to the methods that are applied to the workplace, while the employee is actually working. Off-the-Job methods are used away from the work place. The former means learning while doing, while the latter means learning before doing.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: Apprenticeship programmes put the trainee under the guidance of a ____.

cards.quote: Apprenticeship programmes put the trainee under the guidance of a master worker.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is coaching, as an on-the-job training method?
cards.back: In this method, the superior guides and instructs the trainee as a coach.
cards.quote: In this method, the superior guides and instructs the trainee as a coach.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is internship training?
cards.back: It is a joint programme of training in which educational institutions and business firms cooperate. Selected candidates carry on regular studies for the prescribed period. They also work in some factory or office to acquire practical knowledge and skills.
cards.quote: It is a joint programme of training in which educational institutions and business firms cooperate. Selected candidates carry on regular studies for the prescribed period. They also work in some factory or office to acquire practical knowledge and skills.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is job rotation, as a training method?
cards.back: This kind of training involves shifting the trainee from one department to another or from one job to another. This enables the trainee to gain a broader understanding of all parts of the business and how the organisation as a whole functions.
cards.quote: This kind of training involves shifting the trainee from one department to another or from one job to another. This enables the trainee to gain a broader understanding of all parts of the business and how the organisation as a whole functions.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is the case study method of training?
cards.back: Taken from actual experiences of organisations, cases represent attempts to describe, as accurately as possible real problems that managers have faced. Trainees study the cases to determine problems, analyse causes, develop alternative solutions, select what they believe to be the best solution, and implement it.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is computer modelling, as a training method?
cards.back: It simulates the work environment by programming a computer to imitate some of the realities of the job and allows learning to take place without the risk or high costs that would be incurred if a mistake were made in real life situation.
cards.quote: It simulates the work environment by programming a computer to imitate some of the realities of the job and allows learning to take place without the risk or high costs that would be incurred if a mistake were made in real life situation.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is vestibule training?
cards.back: Employees learn their jobs on the equipment they will be using, but the training is conducted away from the actual work floor. Actual work environments are created in a class room and employees use the same materials, files and equipment.
cards.quote: Employees learn their jobs on the equipment they will be using, but the training is conducted away from the actual work floor. Actual work environments are created in a class room and employees use the same materials, files and equipment.

cards.subject: business_studies
cards.front: What is programmed instruction, as a training method?
cards.back: Information is broken into meaningful units and these units are arranged in a proper way to form a logical and sequential learning package i.e. from simple to complex. The trainee goes through these units by answering questions or filling the blanks.
